Its assessment says so directly (Valid data (content) identifier missing) rather than skipping for want of a graph.

Fabricating a download for a project that has none would earn the points and state something untrue, which ADR-0005 rules out. Describing the files a project does have is the opposite of that, and is what earned them here.

The files carry no MIME type — three points, and this is a data-quality residual. 0803 gained F3-01M and A1-03D like 0868, and gained nothing beyond them. None of its 4,062 files records a mimeType, so no encodingFormat is emitted — a guessed format would be invented — and F-UJI reports NO info about file type available in given metadata for every file it sampled. That fails R1-01MD-2a, which takes R1-01MD-2 and R1-01MD-3 with it, and leaves R1.3-02D with no format list to check. dsp-ingest serves those files as application/octet-stream, so the header fallback does not rescue it either. Both ends would have to change: the export would have to record the MIME type, and ingest would have to serve it. Neither is a change to this code.

No variableMeasured — one point, for every project. R1-01MD-4 asks whether the data content matches the measured variables or observation types the metadata declares, and F-UJI skips it with NO measured variables found in metadata. The DaSCH metadata schema records no such element. This used to be counted under the data-pointer cause, on the strength of its sub-test name; measuring 0868 separated them, because -2 and -3 moved and -4 did not. No data pointer will ever earn it.

ARKs are not registered with DataCite — one point, permanently. F4-01M-1 passes: the metadata is offered through a harvesting endpoint. F4-01M-2 asks for registration in a major research data registry, and the ARKs are DaSCH's own. DaSCH mints no DOIs and will not — every resource carries an ARK, so parity would run to hundreds of thousands of them — so this point is a standing consequence of the identifier scheme rather than an open item; see FAIR Principles.

The deployment published ARKs it does not resolve — one point. A defect, now fixed, not yet re-measured. F1-02D is about a persistent identifier, and F-UJI does find one. It harvested the ARK from the metadata, confirmed the syntax as ark and resolved it successfully (resolvable_status: true). It then discarded it: Landing page domain resolved from PID found in metadata does not match with input URL domain -: run.app <> dasch.swiss, followed by PID syntax is OK but the PID seems to resolve to a different entity, will not use this PID for content negotiation.

This was recorded as an artefact of assessing a non-production host. That reading was wrong. Every deployment emitted the ARK the corpus records regardless of where it was running, so a preview published an identifier that resolves to production — a different deployment, running different code. F-UJI was right to discard it: what it assessed and what the identifier pointed at were two different things. That is the same defect DPE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL fixed one layer down, left in place one layer up.

DPE_ARK_RESOLVER_BASE_URL fixes it. A preview rewrites the host of every emitted ARK to its own and serves the /ark:/ resolver that answers it, so the identifier, the page and the assessed deployment are one thing. Production, DEV and STAGE leave it unset and are unchanged.

No claim is made that F1-02D now passes. Nothing has been re-assessed since the fix, and the columns above are the runs that predate it. Two things are still unknown and are measured, not argued: whether F-UJI's domain comparison is satisfied by a preview that resolves its own ARKs, and what F1-02D does against a dasch.swiss host, which assessing DEV after merge would answer.

A rejected alternative, recorded so it is not re-proposed: serving previews from a *.dasch.swiss host would also satisfy F-UJI's domain comparison, and the assessor would still be sent to production. That moves the metric without fixing anything, which is gaming it.

Two further residuals sit outside this arithmetic, because no F-UJI metric carries them:

  • No metadata persistence policy URL. A persistencePolicy link needs a published policy to point at. FAIR Champion's MetadataPersistence asks for one.
  • Not indexed by a search engine. FAIR Champion's DiscoverableInBing.

FAIR Principles

What DPE does about each of the fifteen FAIR principles, where in the code it happens, and what is not satisfied.

This page is organised by the principles, not by an assessor's metrics. Machine-Readable Metadata records what is emitted and what F-UJI scored for it; those scores appear below only as evidence. A metric code is never the reason a principle is called satisfied. The principles are stable and published; metric numbering is one tool's, and changes when that tool does.

No score is claimed anywhere on this page.

Scope: three different things

FAIR principles are scoped (meta)data. DPE publishes metadata, so the three things below have three different answers and every section keeps them apart.

  • Project metadata — the description of one project's data holdings, served at /dpe/projects/{shortcode}, the page the project's ARK resolves to. This is what DPE publishes, and what a claim below is about unless it says otherwise.
  • Record-level pointers — a project's records appear in its metadata as hasPart entries carrying record ARKs, and the files of fully open records as distribution entries carrying dsp-ingest URLs. Both are bounded prefixes of the record list. Neither is a record landing page.
  • The research data itself — the bitstreams, and everything the VRE holds. DPE does not publish it. It serves metadata only, does not serve a file's bytes and does not redirect to them (OAI-PMH); access to the data is governed outside this repository.

Record landing pages do not exist. RecordGraph is in shared/fair/src/graph.rs, Record is a contract term in the root CONTEXT.md, and both record writers (shared/fair/src/record_datacite.rs, shared/fair/src/record_dublin_core.rs) feed OAI-PMH. But areas/access/dpe/server/src/router.rs registers /dpe/projects/{id} and /dpe/records/{shortcode}/{record_id}/file, and no page route for a record. A record ARK therefore resolves to something outside DPE; what, is not settled in this repository. This is a boundary of what has been built, stated so that no section below reads as though records had pages.

What this page does not assess. The FAIR principles describe (meta)data, not the organisation holding them. Repository trustworthiness — OAIS conformance (root CONTEXT.md), CoreTrustSeal or any other certification — is a separate question with its own criteria, and nothing here is evidence about it either way.

Three kinds of residual

The sections below separate what is not satisfied into three kinds, because they are fixed by three different people.

  • Unbuilt — engineering work nobody has done. A code change fixes it.
  • Data quality — the code is correct and the corpus does not carry the value. The export, or the depositor, fixes it.
  • Institutional — needs a policy, a registration or an organisational decision. No code change fixes it.

The residuals ledger already holds most of the institutional items in their honest form; this page points at them rather than restating them.

A decision already taken is not a residual of any kind. Where one bounds what is reachable, the section says so in its own words and keeps it out of the list — the identifier scheme in F1, what that costs in F4, and DPE being unauthenticated by design in A1.2.

Findable

F1

(meta)data are assigned a globally unique and persistent identifier

Project metadata: yes. Every project has an ARK. canonical_ark in shared/fair/src/project_graph.rs takes the recorded pid when it is neither a Placeholder nor empty, and otherwise builds one from the shortcode. That one value is the schema.org @id and the first identifier entry (render in shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs), the DataCite identifier with identifierType="ARK", the DC.identifier meta tag, and the single cite-as link (project_to_link_set in shared/fair/src/signposting.rs). Records carry ARKs of their own (RecordGraph::ark, shared/fair/src/graph.rs).

The ARK path is never rewritten. areas/access/dpe/core/src/ark.rs normalises only the host, and only on a deployment that publishes ARKs naming itself.

The data: no. A bitstream has no identifier of its own. It is named by a dsp-ingest URL, in distribution.contentUrl and as downloadUrl from the file-metadata endpoint. A URL is a location, and that location has a retirement date (Machine-Readable Metadata).

A settled non-goal, not a residual. The scheme is ARK throughout, and DaSCH mints no DOIs. The reason is granularity and cost: every resource carries an ARK, so DOI parity would mean hundreds of thousands of DOIs, which is prohibitively expensive. That is a decision taken rather than a task outstanding, and it is why no section of this page treats a DOI as something missing. F4 records where it bites.

Not satisfied

  • Bitstreams have no persistent identifier. Unbuilt.
  • An ARK is persistent because DaSCH goes on resolving it. That is an organisational commitment, and nothing in this code makes it one. Institutional.

F2

data are described with rich metadata (defined by R1 below)

What DPE does. A project file has 37 members (root CONTEXT.md). ProjectGraph::build in shared/fair/src/project_graph.rs resolves them into one graph: titles and alternative names, description and abstract, keywords, disciplines, creators and contributors with their ORCID and GND identifiers and resolved affiliations, start and end dates, temporal coverage resolved to W3CDTF ranges, spatial coverage, data language, licences, access rights, funding, publications, the project website, a how-to-cite string, status, and the part list. Every representation is a projection of that one graph.

Where. ProjectGraph::build; project_to_schema_org (shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs); project_to_datacite and project_to_datacite_json; project_to_dublin_core and project_to_dublin_core_meta.

Not satisfied

  • Eight recorded fields reach no machine-readable representation. ProjectRaw (shared/metadata/src/project.rs) carries provenance, data_management_plan, contact_point, type_of_data, short_description, documentation_material, additional_material and image_credit; none of them appears anywhere in shared/fair/src outside its test fixtures, and ProjectGraph has no field for any of them. The human page renders several — provenance_card in areas/access/dpe/web/src/pages/project/components/project_details_tabs/dataset_overview_section/mod.rs, the DMP and contact point in areas/access/dpe/web/src/pages/project/components/project_sidebar/mod.rs. A machine therefore sees less than a person does. clusters and collections are absent the same way; they are I3's point rather than this one. type_of_data is the consequential one: the project's DataCite resourceType is the constant "Research Project" and resourceTypeGeneral the constant "Project" (shared/fair/src/datacite.rs), so the recorded kind of the data never reaches a representation. Unbuilt.
  • The DaSCH metadata schema records no variable or observation-type element, so nothing maps to variableMeasured. Data quality, at the schema level. (Evidence: R1-01MD-4 in the residuals ledger.)
  • How rich the metadata is varies per project. A field the corpus records as a Placeholder yields no key at all (helpers::real), which is truthful and also means F2 is answered differently for different projects.

F3

metadata clearly and explicitly include the identifier of the data it describes

The project's own identifier: yes. The ARK is both @id and the first identifier entry, and url carries the landing page beside it (render in shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs).

The identifiers of its records: partly. part_nodes emits one Dataset node per record with the record's ARK as @id, but only over a prefix: 100 entries in the embedded block (HAS_PART_CAP in areas/access/dpe/server/src/metadata.rs) and as many as fit 4,000,000 bytes in /metadata.jsonld (JSON_LD_BYTE_BUDGET). The complete list is the OAI set project:{shortcode}, reachable from the document in two hops over links it already carries.

Pointers to the bitstreams: a location, not an identifier. distribution_nodes emits one DataDownload per file of a listed record, with contentUrl, and only for a record the corpus records as Full Open Access (publishable_file in shared/fair/src/graph.rs). hasPart and distribution take the same prefix in the same order, so the files described are the files of the records listed.

Evidence, not the claim: F3-01M moved from 0/1 to 1/1 for the two projects whose records carry files once distribution was emitted; see the assessment results.

Not satisfied

  • What the metadata includes for a bitstream is a retrieval URL, not an identifier, and that URL names a host with a retirement date. Unbuilt (a DPE-owned stable download URL is considered and rejected in Machine-Readable Metadata; it is an ADR question).
  • Files of records the corpus does not record as fully open are not pointed at at all. That is ADR-0005's decision rather than a defect, and it does mean F3 is unanswered for those records.

F4

(meta)data are registered or indexed in a searchable resource

What DPE does. Two routes, neither of which needs a DOI.

  • Harvesting. DPE is an OAI-PMH 2.0 data provider at /dpe/oai (areas/access/dpe/api-oai/): all six verbs, oai_dc and oai_datacite, and selective harvesting over the sets project:{shortcode} and cluster:{id}. Any aggregator can take the whole corpus. F-UJI's F4-01M-1 passes on this alone.
  • Search-engine indexing. The embedded schema.org Dataset block is the form Google Dataset Search ingests, and at 3.7% of Googlebot's 2 MB crawl budget for the largest committed project it has room (Machine-Readable Metadata). The project graph also names the catalogue it belongs to, as includedInDataCatalog.

Where. areas/access/dpe/server/src/router.rs (/dpe/oai), areas/access/dpe/api-oai/src/handlers/, OAI-PMH; render in shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs for includedInDataCatalog.

A permanent limit, from the identifier scheme. DaSCH mints no DOIs, for the reason F1 records, and registration in a DOI-based registry therefore does not happen. F4-01M-2 asks for registration in a major research-data registry, and in the pinned F-UJI image DataCite is the only one of the three routes actually queried — Mendeley fails DNS resolution inside the container and the Google Search cache database ships empty, so that sub-test is partly a property of how the container is provisioned (docs/specs/2026-09-15-fair-metadata-exposure/01-feat-fair-metadata-exposure-plan-journal.md). DataCite registration is keyed on a DOI prefix. So as F-UJI measures F4 there is a ceiling, it follows from the identifier decision, and no work on this code moves it. It is not an open item.

Not satisfied

  • Being indexable is not being indexed. DPE serves no sitemap; nothing in the tree advertises the catalogue to a crawler, which then has to find every project page by following links. Unbuilt.
  • Not indexed by a search engine. Institutional. (Evidence: FAIR Champion's DiscoverableInBing.)

Accessible

A1

(meta)data are retrievable by their identifier using a standardized communications protocol

Project metadata: yes. The ARK resolves by HTTP redirect to the landing page. In production the resolver is ark.dasch.swiss; a deployment that publishes ARKs naming itself mounts its own (areas/access/dpe/server/src/ark.rs::resolve_project, registered in router.rs only when DPE_ARK_RESOLVER_BASE_URL is set). The page carries its metadata inline, and two machine-readable representations sit beside it at their own URLs, reachable directly or by a single 303 when Accept prefers one (landing_page in areas/access/dpe/server/src/metadata.rs, over the decision table in shared/fair/src/negotiate.rs). Every answer from that route carries Vary: Accept (project_page_handler in areas/access/dpe/server/src/shell.rs). OAI-PMH is a second retrieval protocol over the same metadata.

The data: not from DPE. DPE serves metadata only. A consumer reads downloadUrl from /dpe/records/{shortcode}/{record_id}/file (areas/access/dpe/server/src/downloads.rs) and then fetches the bytes from dsp-ingest itself.

Not satisfied

  • Nothing in DPE retrieves data by its identifier, because no bitstream has one (F1). What it offers is retrieval by location.

A1.1

the protocol is open, free, and universally implementable

What DPE does. HTTP throughout, and OAI-PMH 2.0 over HTTP. No client library, no key, no account, no registration: DPE is the public, unauthenticated, read-only server of the Access Area (areas/access/CONTEXT.md). The representation routes and /dpe/oai share a per-IP rate limit (rate_limited_router in areas/access/dpe/server/src/router.rs, DPE_OAI_RATE_LIMIT_*), which bounds request rate and gates nothing.

Not satisfied. Nothing identified. This is the one section with no residual, and it is the cheapest of the fifteen to satisfy.

A1.2

the protocol allows for an authentication and authorization procedure, where necessary

This section is the one most easily answered with the wrong evidence, so the wrong evidence is named first.

What DPE does, and what it does not mean. DPE publishes access conditions: isAccessibleForFree and conditionsOfAccess in the schema.org graph, and DC.accessRights as a COAR access-right URI (helpers::coar_access_right). It also withholds the file pointer of any record the corpus does not record as Full Open Access (publishable_file in shared/fair/src/graph.rs). None of that is an authentication or authorization procedure. publishable_file's own documentation says so: it governs what is published, not what is reachable — dsp-ingest serves those URLs to anyone holding one, and DPE's own file-metadata endpoint returns the same URL for any record with a file.

DPE itself needs no procedure: everything it serves is published metadata. Authorization, where it is necessary, lives outside this repository — in the VRE, in dsp-ingest, and in the Deposit Area, whose editor has its own (Authentication). That is the producer side, not access to published data.

Not answered by DPE

  • DPE implements no authenticated path to restricted data, and does not mediate access to it by any procedure. HTTP would allow one; nothing here uses it. That is a boundary rather than a residual — areas/access/CONTEXT.md defines DPE as the public, unauthenticated, read-only server — and whether the Access Area should offer one is a question no decision record answers yet.

A2

metadata are accessible, even when the data are no longer available

What DPE does. Metadata availability does not depend on bitstream availability. DPE serves the committed corpus under areas/access/dpe/server/data/ rather than reading the archive, and a project whose records carry no file has a complete landing page all the same — 081C, with 27,026 records and not one file, is the worked case (assessment results).

That is a property of today's deployment, not a commitment. The rest of this section is what is missing.

Not satisfied. This is the weakest of the fifteen.

  • No tombstone. A shortcode that names no project gets an always-200 "Project Not Found" page (landing_page in areas/access/dpe/server/src/metadata.rs) — not a 410 Gone carrying the metadata of what used to be there. Nothing in the tree distinguishes "never existed" from "withdrawn". Unbuilt.
  • OAI-PMH says so out loud. Identify advertises <deletedRecord>no</deletedRecord> (OaiXmlBuilder::write_identify in areas/access/dpe/api-oai/src/xml.rs), which tells a harvester the repository maintains no information about deletions. Unbuilt.
  • No metadata persistence policy to point a persistencePolicy link at. Institutional. (Evidence: FAIR Champion's MetadataPersistence.)

Interoperable

I1

(meta)data use a formal, accessible, shared, and broadly applicable language for knowledge representation.

What DPE does. JSON-LD, twice: embedded in the page head as <script type="application/ld+json"> and standalone at /dpe/projects/{shortcode}/metadata.jsonld. The @context is https://schema.org plus a prov: binding (render in shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs). Beside it, DataCite kernel 4 as JSON and as XML, and Dublin Core as <meta> tags and as oai_dc. An assessor reads the JSON-LD as RDF, which is why several property shapes are node objects rather than strings (Machine-Readable Metadata).

Where. shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs (render, script_safe_json); areas/access/dpe/server/src/metadata.rs (render, project_json_ld); shared/fair/src/datacite_json.rs; shared/fair/src/dublin_core_meta.rs.

Not satisfied

  • No Turtle and no RDF/XML. ADR-0005 leaves Turtle open ("if it earns its place") and it has not been served. A consumer wanting RDF runs the JSON-LD through a processor. Unbuilt, deliberately deferred.
  • The JSON-LD representation is a bounded prefix and does not say so. schema.org has no property meaning "this collection is partial"; Hydra's totalItems was considered and rejected. A consumer reading the document alone cannot tell; one that follows its links can recover the complete list. The reasoning is in A byte budget.

I2

(meta)data use vocabularies that follow FAIR principles

What DPE does. Published, versioned, resolvable vocabularies throughout:

VocabularyUsed forWhere
schema.orgthe root graph and every node in itshared/fair/src/schema_org.rs
Dublin Core elements<meta name="DC.*"> and the oai_dc recordshared/fair/src/dublin_core_meta.rs, dublin_core.rs
DataCite kernel 4metadata.datacite.json and oai_dataciteshared/fair/src/datacite.rs, datacite_json.rs
PROV-Oprov:wasAttributedToPROV_NAMESPACE, attributed_to in schema_org.rs
SPDXlicence identifiers (rightsIdentifierScheme="SPDX")shared/fair/src/datacite.rs, helpers::license_identifier_to_label
COAR access rightsDC.accessRightshelpers::coar_access_right
ORCID, GNDagent identifiersperson_to_agent in shared/fair/src/resolve.rs
GND, STW, LCSH, AATsubject schemes, inferred from an authority URLhelpers::infer_subject_scheme
ChronOntology, W3CDTFtemporal coverage and its resolved rangesshared_metadata::temporal_coverage
FAIR Signposting (level 1)the typed link setshared/fair/src/signposting.rs
OAI-PMH 2.0the harvesting protocolareas/access/dpe/api-oai/

Evidence, not the claim: I2-01M moved from 0/1 to 1/1 when PROV was added, because F-UJI's linked-data registry lists that namespace.

Not satisfied

  • Contributor roles are free text. CONTRIBUTOR_ROLES in shared/metadata/src/project.rs is documented as "an offer, not a constraint", and the committed data spells the same role several ways, crams several into one entry, and uses prose in place of a role. helpers::map_contributor_type maps what it recognises onto DataCite's vocabulary and falls back to Other. Data quality.
  • Organizations have no identifier. resolve_agent gives an organization name_identifiers: vec![], and an affiliation is emitted as an Organization name with nothing else (agent_node in schema_org.rs). No ROR. The organization files carry a homepage and a postal address and no persistent identifier (areas/access/dpe/server/data/organizations/). Unbuilt, and data quality behind it.
  • Person identifiers are sparse, and two are typed away. 96 of the 416 committed person files record "type": "ORCID" in sameAs. Two more hold an orcid.org URL typed "URL" (person-146, person-246); person_to_agent matches on the type string, so those two agents get no @id, no author link and no prov:wasAttributedTo entry although the identifier is there. Every section below that depends on an agent IRI inherits this. Data quality.
  • Keywords are free text, and disciplines carry a subject scheme only where the corpus records an authority URL.

I3

(meta)data include qualified references to other (meta)data

What DPE does. This is the best-served of the fifteen.

  • A record's DataCite record relates it to its project: relationType="IsPartOf", relatedIdentifierType="ARK" (record_to_datacite in shared/fair/src/record_datacite.rs).
  • The project's schema.org graph carries hasPart over record ARKs (part_nodes), citation nodes whose @id is a publication's PID when one is recorded (citation_nodes), spatialCoverage Place nodes with sameAs to an authority URL (spatial_nodes), agent nodes whose @id is the agent's ORCID (agent_node), prov:wasAttributedTo pointing at those same nodes rather than describing copies (attributed_to), includedInDataCatalog, and sameAs to the recorded PID when it differs from the resolved ARK.
  • The Signposting set adds cite-as, one describedby per representation, author per ORCID, and license when exactly one applies; each representation answers with describes back at the page (representation_to_link_set).

Not satisfied

  • A project's DataCite record carries no relatedIdentifiers at all. shared/fair/src/datacite.rs holds the unfilled note: RelatedIdentifiers — should contain parent Project Cluster ARK. TODO: Populate once Project Cluster data is available. So a project's cluster membership, its records and its publications are all absent from the DataCite representations, although the schema.org graph carries the last two. Unbuilt.
  • A reference to an agent is qualified only when that agent has an ORCID. One without stays a blank node and is left out of prov:wasAttributedTo entirely — naming some agents does not deny the others, but it does mean the reference is unqualified for most of them (see I2).
  • Nothing relates one project to another, although Clusters and Collections exist and are served as OAI sets. Unbuilt.

Reusable

R1

meta(data) are richly described with a plurality of accurate and relevant attributes

(Quoted as published; the paper's Box 2 reads meta(data) here.)

What DPE does. The attribute list is F2's. What R1 adds is accurate, and three rules carry that:

  • Nothing is invented for a score (ADR-0005). No representation asserts a fact the corpus does not record.
  • A Placeholder yields no key. helpers::real is the test every writer that must not assert a falsehood applies to a corpus string; MISSING never reaches a <meta> tag or a JSON-LD value.
  • One resolved graph feeds every representation, so two of them cannot disagree — asserted for every committed project by every_representation_of_a_committed_object_agrees_with_the_others in dpe-api-oai.

Not satisfied

  • The eight unemitted fields of F2. Unbuilt.
  • No variable or observation-type element exists to describe. Data quality, at the schema level.
  • Two mandatory-field fallbacks are not facts, and a consumer cannot tell. DataCite makes publicationYear and at least one creator mandatory, so the representations that rule governs fall back to the year 2015 (FALLBACK_PUBLICATION_YEAR in shared/fair/src/graph.rs) and to an organizational DaSCH (creators_with_fallback). Both are reached only through those named helpers, and schema.org's optional datePublished deliberately omits the key instead — but a consumer reading a DataCite record for a project that records no usable date reads 2015 as though it were recorded. Data quality: the fallback fires only where the corpus records no usable value, and DataCite's mandatory field leaves the writer no way to mark one as supplied.

R1.1

(meta)data are released with a clear and accessible data usage license

The data: yes, where the corpus records a licence. license as a node object {"@id": <SPDX URI>} in the schema.org graph — a node and not a string, because schema.org's remote context does not coerce license to @id and a consumer asking for a licence resource would find none. Beside it: DC.rights, DataCite rightsList with rightsIdentifierScheme="SPDX", a Signposting license link, and a license on each DataDownload carrying the record's own licence, which across the corpus is not always the project's.

The metadata: no. Nothing in this tree licenses the metadata records themselves. Identify emits repositoryName, baseURL, protocolVersion, adminEmail, earliestDatestamp, deletedRecord and granularity, and no rights block (OaiXmlBuilder::write_identify). No landing page says anything about reuse of the metadata. A harvester taking oai_dc records away has no licence for them.

Not satisfied

  • The metadata has no licence. This needs a decision first and one field after. Institutional.
  • A project that records no licence emits no license key — truthful, and R1.1 is then unanswered for that project. Data quality.
  • A project licensed several ways gets no Signposting license link at all, because the profile allows at most one and has no way to say "these apply together" (project_to_link_set). The JSON-LD still lists them.

R1.2

(meta)data are associated with detailed provenance

What DPE does. prov:wasAttributedTo over DaSCH and every credited creator that has an ORCID, with prov: bound in the @context (PROV_NAMESPACE and attributed_to in shared/fair/src/schema_org.rs). Nothing new is asserted: creator and publisher already name those agents, and PROV-O restates the relation in the vocabulary a consumer asking about provenance reads. Beside it: producer as a ResearchProject with start and end dates and members (producer_node), funder and funding as MonetaryGrant nodes, datePublished where a year is recorded, and DataCite's Created, Issued and Collected dates.

Evidence, not the claim: R1.2-01M moved from 1/2 to 2/2 on the run that added PROV.

Not satisfied

  • The project's recorded provenance statement is not emitted anywhere machine-readable. ProjectRaw.provenance is free text, the human page renders it as a card (provenance_card), and no shared-fair writer reads it. The one field named for this principle is the one the machine-readable metadata leaves out. Unbuilt.
  • Nothing records the provenance of the metadata. ProjectRaw carries no created or modified date (shared/metadata/src/project.rs), so who curated a project's description, when, and through what revision is not recorded and cannot be emitted. Records do carry date_created and date_modified (RecordGraph); projects do not. Unbuilt, and a contract change before it is a writer change.
  • prov:generatedAtTime is deliberately not emitted: the corpus records a publication year, not a generation time, so the statement would be approximately true at best (Provenance).
  • A creator without an ORCID is not attributed, because there is no node to point at (see I2 for how many that is).

R1.3

(meta)data meet domain-relevant community standards

What DPE does. The general research-data standards are met and checked:

  • DataCite kernel 4, schemaVersion 4.6, datacentreSymbol DASCH.DSP. The JSON is validated against DataCite's own JSON schema and the XML against datacite-kernel-4.xsd for every committed project, by the corpus-wide test in dpe-api-oai.
  • OAI-PMH 2.0, validated against OAI-PMH.xsd.
  • Dublin Core, schema.org Dataset (the shape Google Dataset Search reads), FAIR Signposting level 1, COAR access rights, SPDX, W3CDTF.

Not satisfied

  • No humanities-domain standard is served. No representation offers TEI, CIDOC-CRM, EAD or CMDI. The corpus records XML (TEI) as a typeOfData value (general_data_type in shared/fair/src/graph.rs), so content in one of those standards is described by metadata that does not speak it. Unbuilt.
  • File formats are described only where the export records a MIME type. encodingFormat is omitted rather than guessed. All 4,062 files of project 0803 carry no mimeType, and dsp-ingest serves them as application/octet-stream, so neither end supplies it. Data quality, at both ends. (Evidence: R1.3-02D.)

Sources

The principle wording quoted above is Box 2 of:

Wilkinson, M. D. et al. "The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship". Scientific Data 3, 160018 (2016). https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18

GO FAIR restates the same fifteen principles with a commentary on each, at https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/.

The assessors named in the evidence notes are separate from the principles. F-UJI's metrics are cited in its own result payload as https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6461229; FAIR Champion's indicators are defined in the FAIR Maturity Indicators index. What each of them scored, when, and against what, is in Machine-Readable Metadata.

Config Language

How a project's config.kdl is structured, how it composes components, and how the engine validates it. Reads on top of dsp-incubator cpe/docs/COMPONENT_LIBRARY.md (the components this file invokes) and dsp-incubator cpe/docs/adr/0006-config-language-kdl.md (why KDL).

The language is implemented in cpe-core, at areas/access/cpe/core. A change to the language changes this document in the same PR.

"Boot", "hard-fail" and "the web binary" in this document. The text was written for a binary that validated every project when it started and exited on an error. Here a project's configuration is validated at the project's Activation (areas/access/cpe/CONTEXT.md). So "at boot" reads "at the project's Activation", and a "hard-fail", or "boot fails", reads: the project is not served and its paths answer 503; the process and the other projects are unaffected. "The web binary" reads "the page assembly and its host crate" (cpe-web, cpe-server). The --check flag and the cpe command are the incubator binary's; neither exists here.

The KDL primer (just enough)

KDL is "JSON for documents". One node per line; positional arguments separated by whitespace; named attributes as key=value; children in braces. Comments with // (line) or /- (node).

node-name "positional-arg" attribute="value" {
    child-node "another-arg"
    /- commented-out-child
}

That's the whole syntax CPE needs. The full KDL spec has more (slashdashes for arguments, raw strings, type annotations); the engine ignores constructs it doesn't need.

KDL v6 literals: booleans and null are written #true, #false, and #null — not bare true/false/null. CPE's v1 config schema doesn't currently use boolean or null values directly, but the where node (data-binding, see below) may accept equals=#true. Authors copying examples from pre-v6 KDL docs will see a parse error if they use the bare form.

Property names in KDL are unquoted identifiers in most cases. If a property name contains hyphens (per-page, show-properties), KDL allows it. If it has weird characters, use a string.

Top-level structure

Every config.kdl has exactly one site block, an optional top-level labels block, an optional top-level remodel block, plus one or more page blocks:

site {
    title "Incunabula"
    description "Early printed books from the 15th century"
    languages "de" "en"
    nav {
        item label="Home" route="/"
        item label="Books" route="/books"
    }
    chrome {
        // chrome translations — see "Translations" below
    }
    theme {
        // CSS variable overrides — see "Theming" below
    }
}

labels {
    // property/class display-label translations — see "`labels` block" below
}

remodel {
    // how the archive's snapshot becomes this project's store — see
    // "`remodel` block" below
}

page id="home" route="/" {
    // page body
}

page id="books" route="/books" {
    // page body
}

labels is optional and top-level — a sibling of site and page, not nested inside site {} (unlike chrome, which genuinely is a site child). A project that declares no labels block gets identical behaviour to today: every property/class display label falls back to humanize_property_name.

remodel is optional and top-level too, and a file holds at most one: a second remodel node is UnexpectedTopLevelNode. It is the store builder's input; the web binary validates it and does not use it. A project without one (hdm, alice-in-daschland) validates as before.

site block

Project-level metadata and chrome.

Required:

  • title — project display name. Used in <title>, the brand lockup, the breadcrumb's project crumb, the 404s and the site index. Chrome-id-or-literal (like description): a value that matches a declared chrome { string } id renders that string's translation for the request language; any other value renders verbatim in every language (Alice, HdM). A literal that happens to equal a declared chrome id is translated — the same accepted risk as description. The site index resolves it per declared language and falls back to en, then to the project's default language, for an undeclared one.
  • languages — list of ISO 639-1 codes. Must include at least de and en for v1 (per cpe-poc.md §9.2). A project MAY declare additional languages beyond this floor (e.g. Alice declares en/de/fr/it) provided chrome-string completeness holds (every declared chrome string must carry every declared language — boot hard-fail otherwise). Per-language narrative variant files are optional (Phase 3.9) — a narrative file must resolve to either the base file or the default-language variant (boot hard-fail otherwise, NarrativeFileNotFound); non-default-language variants may be added incrementally without authoring every language up front (see Translations below for the render-time fallback chain). Record-page property values without a source translation for the additional language fall back gracefully to the first-present value via CPE's pick_values chain.

Optional:

  • description — short prose for the site index and metadata. Like a nav item's label (see below), the value is chrome-string id OR literal — if it exactly matches a declared chrome-string id, the renderer resolves it to that id's translation for the current request language; otherwise it renders as-is. This lets a project supply a translated description via the chrome {} block (see Alice's site-description chrome string). Rendered in the per-project footer and, per-project, as the teaser text on the site index's project card.
  • cover-image — a plain relative path to a cover asset inside the project's own directory, e.g. "assets/cover.webp". Unlike description/eyebrow/image-credit, this is not chrome-id-or-literal — the value is a path, never translated, and used as-is for every language. Validation: must be a plain relative path with no .. segment and no leading / (hard-fail, DiagnosticKind::InvalidCoverImagePath), and must resolve to a file that actually exists under the project's embedded assets/ directory once the project is discovered (hard-fail, DiagnosticKind::CoverImageNotFound). A missing assets/ directory is not an exemption: declaring a cover-image when the project has no assets/ directory at all is the same hard-fail, since the truthful answer to "does this file exist?" is still no. Served at runtime via the engine-reserved /{project-id}/_assets/{*path} route under CPE's base (see "Route patterns" below) — a site index's project-card <img src> is <base>/<project-id>/_assets/<cover-image path>. Absent → the site-index card shows a same-height imageless ghost slot instead of a broken image.
  • image-credit — credit/rights line shown under the cover image on the site index's project card (e.g. "Foto: Alberto Venzago", or "Authorship: AI-Generated." for a synthetic asset). Like description, the value is chrome-id-or-literal — if it exactly matches a declared chrome-string id, the renderer resolves it to that id's translation for the current request language; otherwise it renders as-is. No existence validation beyond parsing. Absent → the card's reserved credit-caption row renders empty (the row is always reserved, so card titles still align across a grid row).
  • eyebrow — a short scent line (material · place · span) shown above the title on the site-index's project card, e.g. "Showcase · EN · DE". Chrome-id-or-literal, same idiom as description/image-credit. No existence validation beyond parsing. Absent → the card's reserved eyebrow line renders empty (the project's <base>/<project-id>/ path in the card's footer row still identifies it, so no card loses its identity).
  • default-language — one of languages. Default: first listed.
  • nav — top navigation items (see below).
  • chrome — translations for static UI strings (see below).
  • theme — CSS variable overrides (see below).
  • footer-attribution, not-found — the two project copy overrides (see "Project copy overrides" below).

cover-image/image-credit/eyebrow are all optional and purely additive — they affect only the cross-project site index's project-card presentation, never a project's own pages. The site index is CPE's overview of its projects, the page at its base (<base>/): cpe-server serves it and cpe_web::page::render_site_index renders it, from cpe_web::project::Project::teaser. Alice's config.kdl is the worked example:

site {
    title "Alice in DaSCHland"
    cover-image "assets/cover.webp"
    image-credit "Authorship: AI-Generated."
    eyebrow "site-eyebrow"
    // ...
    chrome {
        string "site-eyebrow" {
            en "Showcase · EN · DE · FR · IT"
            de "Schaufenster · EN · DE · FR · IT"
            fr "Vitrine · EN · DE · FR · IT"
            it "Vetrina · EN · DE · FR · IT"
        }
    }
}

Project copy overrides: footer-attribution, not-found (Incunabula Slice 8 / G11)

site {
    footer-attribution "footer-credit"     // chrome-id-or-literal
    not-found {
        browse route="/books"
        browse route="/woodcuts" label="nf-woodcuts"   // label= optional
        browse route="/strips"
    }
}

This is a narrow, deliberate exception to the chrome-localization rule that "engine UI strings live in the catalog, not per-project config" (docs/plans/chrome-localization/implementation-plan.md). Exactly two pieces of engine copy are project-overridable: the project 404's browse links (owner decision O5) and the footer attribution (Slice 8 decision 9). Nothing else is; a new override needs its own owner decision, not a precedent read off this one. (A third, the settings page's lede, went with the settings page, general chrome D2, 2026-10-08.)

  • footer-attribution — replaces the footer's attribution line. The value is chrome-id-or-literal and renders as plain text. Absent: the engine's attribution string.
  • not-found { browse route="…" label="…" } — the project 404 page's "Or browse:" links, in declaration order. Each route must match a declared page route exactly, the same rule as a nav item's route (hard-fail, UnresolvedNotFoundBrowseRoute). At most three browse entries are allowed, the design cap (hard-fail, TooManyNotFoundBrowseLinks). label= is optional and chrome-id-or-literal (a declared chrome-string id renders its translation; any other value renders verbatim — so there is no boot check on it). Absent, the link reads the label of the nav item with the same route, and failing that the route itself. With no browse entries at all, the 404 lists the first three nav items, as before.

Validation: a non-string footer-attribution argument is InvalidFieldType. A browse with no route is MissingRequiredAttribute. A wrong-typed route or label is InvalidAttributeType, never a silently dropped link. All of these are config-internal. Absent config changes nothing (dsp-incubator cpe/docs/adr/0002-deployment-topology.md).

Both are rendered: footer-attribution in the shared footer (web/src/page.rs), and not-found { browse } on the project 404 page (areas/access/cpe/components/src/component/resource_detail.rs).

date-precision-word (Incunabula Slice 8, decision 4)

site {
    date-precision-word #true   // KDL bool; default #false
}

A single optional boolean site {} child, opt-in and off by default. When #true, every rendered Date property value on a record/reader page (never in a browse row's gloss) gets a trailing precision word appended after the date text in a span.prec inside span.v-date — the localized word for the value's DatePrecision (Tag/Monat/Jahr, DE; day/month/year, EN), or Zeitraum/range when the value is a genuine range (ir::date_is_range). When the value's stored calendar is Gregorian and its precision is day or month, a calendar word is appended after the precision word, separated by · (e.g. Tag · gregorianisch, month · Gregorian; never at year precision, where Julian and Gregorian share one year count) — Julian and an absent calendar are the unmarked case and add nothing (owner decision 5: Julian is Incunabula's default calendar, so marking it everywhere would be noisier than marking the exception).

Incunabula's config.kdl sets date-precision-word #true; the word is resolved by format_date in areas/access/cpe/components/src/component/resource_detail.rs from the boot-lowered SiteConfig.date_precision_word (read from site in render_component and passed via ResourceDetailCfg.date_precision_word, web/src/page.rs, and CompoundViewerCfg.date_precision_word — NOT threaded through RenderContext), using the ChromeMsg::DatePrec{Day,Month,Year,Range} / ChromeMsg::CalendarGregorian catalog entries.

Validation: a non-boolean argument (e.g. date-precision-word "yes") is InvalidFieldType, never a silent false. Absent, or a bare date-precision-word node with no argument, lowers to false — the project's dates render exactly as before this feature existed.

narrative-companion, narrative-side and text-align (layout pass)

site {
    narrative-companion "rail"   // "rail" (default) or "text"
    narrative-side "end"         // "end" (default) or "start"
    text-align "justify"         // "start" (default) or "justify"
}
  • narrative-companion and narrative-side are the project's defaults for the narrative layout; a page's first narrative can override either (see "narrative: companion= and side=" below). rail shows the "On this page" list beside the intro from 80rem; text shows none. side is the edge the rail stands at. No shipped project sets either.
  • text-align "justify" justifies and hyphenates the project's narrative prose and book introductions (a prose block's own paragraphs; the lede, lists, quotes, glosses and invite lists stay ragged), and only where the column is at least 30rem wide, so a phone stays ragged. It is emitted as <html data-align="justify">; "start" emits nothing. Incunabula sets it. Justified text departs from WCAG 1.4.8 (level AAA, which asks for text that is not justified). CPE targets AA; this is an owner opt-in per project. Hyphenation follows the page's <html lang>, so a quotation in another language is divided by the page's rules.

Validation: a non-string argument is InvalidFieldType; a string outside the key's two values is UnknownSiteValue { key, value, allowed } (Error). All three are config-internal.

nav

nav {
    item label="Home" route="/"
    item label="Books" route="/books"
    item label="About" route="/about"
}

Each item has a label (translated chrome string id or literal) and a route (must match a declared page route, leading slash relative to the project root). Rendered as a <nav> on every page.

Validation: every nav route must match a declared page route exactly (hard-fail, DiagnosticKind::UnresolvedNavRoute, Phase 3.8) — exact string equality.

The renderer's aria-current active-page highlight (nav_item_is_active) is a different, broader comparison: it marks a nav item current on an exact route match, and also on any of that item's nested routes (the current path starting with item + "/"), except for the home route /, which never prefix-matches. This lets a Books nav item stay highlighted on /books/:id, not just on /books itself.

Additionally: a nav item's label is chrome-string id OR literal (see chrome below) — if it exactly matches a declared chrome-string id, the renderer prefers the chrome translation over the literal text. That is the intended bilingual-nav idiom, and it is not diagnosed: a NavLabelChromeIdCollision Warning used to fire on it (14 across the three shipped projects) but could not distinguish the idiom from an accidental collision, because the only ids it compared against were ones the project itself declared. It was removed as boot-log noise.

chrome

Static UI strings (button labels, facet titles, system messages) that need translation. Keyed strings, one per language:

chrome {
    string "search-placeholder" {
        de "Suche..."
        en "Search..."
    }
    string "facet-publisher" {
        de "Verlag"
        en "Publisher"
    }
}

Components reference chrome strings by id (e.g. search-bar placeholder="search-placeholder").

Validation: every chrome string must have an entry for every declared site language. Missing translation is a hard-fail at boot.

theme

Enumerated per-project visual design knob, optional (defaults apply when the block is absent):

theme {
    accent "ochre"        // ochre | green | teal | red   (default: ochre)
    background "tint"     // neutral | tint               (default: tint)
    typeface "newsreader" // one of 11 faces (default: newsreader) — see below
}

The engine validates the declared values at boot (hard-fail on any unrecognised value) and emits them as HTML attributes on <html>:

KeyAllowed valuesEmitted attribute
accentochre, green, teal, reddata-accent="ochre"
backgroundneutral, tintdata-bg="tint"
typefaceone of 11 faces (below)data-pick="newsreader"

The typeface value is the data-pick face name. The 11 faces, grouped here as the design tool's Tweaks panel groups them (the grouping is not part of the value):

  • Bookish (serif-led): newsreader, garamond, crimson
  • Balanced (incl. serif-title / sans-body pairings): spectral, lora, literata, spectral-figtree, newsreader-figtree
  • Casual (sans-led): figtree, hanken, schibsted

⚠️ A mockup's Tweaks typeface is a voice, not a face. A Claude Design mockup's Tweaks panel exposes typeface as one of the voices above (e.g. bookish), while theme { typeface } accepts only the concrete face names this table lists. Transcribing a mockup's Tweaks value verbatim is an unrecognised value — a boot hard-fail, and per dsp-incubator cpe/docs/adr/0002-deployment-topology.md's single-binary topology one project's invalid config takes the whole deployment down. Map the voice to its default face instead (bookish → newsreader), and expect the same voice-vs-face mismatch on any Tweaks value you transcribe into config. The table above is the authority for the accepted faces.

The data-direction attribute is always "edition" (fixed, not a project knob). The data-appearance attribute (light / dark) is resolved from the user's cookie or ?appearance= query parameter — it is a global user/reading preference (toggled in the header), not a per-project knob, so it is not part of theme {}.

The design-system tokens.css defines token overrides keyed on these data attributes.

No request-time override. The theme {} block is the only source of these attributes; no query key or cookie changes them. The settings page that once previewed them live was removed (general chrome, D2, 2026-10-08). A request still carrying one of its retired query keys (accent, background, typeface, reset) is answered with a 303 to the same URL without them.

The _-prefixed route namespace is reserved for engine-registered routes (_static, _assets, the _<component> fragment segments): a config page must not declare a route whose first segment starts with _ (boot hard-fail, DiagnosticKind::ReservedRoute).

(An earlier image route reservation and _zoom fragment segment, for a since-rejected-and-removed deep-zoom viewer-state surface, no longer exist either — see dsp-incubator cpe/docs/adr/0008-images-are-embedded-only-resources.md's post-implementation note. The embedded-media plan's plate column and its _plate fragment endpoint are gone too — see the record-viewer entry in CLAUDE.md's Current state section.)

labels block

A top-level block (a sibling of site and page, not nested inside site {}) declaring per-language display labels for properties and classes — a direct analog of the chrome { string } mechanism above, but keyed by property/class name rather than an arbitrary id:

labels {
    property "role" {
        en "Role"
        de "Rolle"
        fr "Rôle"
        it "Ruolo"
    }
    class "Character" {
        en "Character"
        de "Figur"
        fr "Personnage"
        it "Personaggio"
    }
}

Each property/class child names a property or Class (matching the same strings used elsewhere in config — show-properties, facet property, resource-detail class="…") and carries one string per language, exactly like chrome { string }.

Fallback contract. A declared label wins; where no label is declared for a given property or class, the engine falls back to the pre-existing humanize_property_name behaviour (the same title-casing/--and-_-splitting transform that was the only source of these labels before this mechanism existed). This means a project can declare labels for some properties/classes and rely on humanization for the rest — there is no all-or-nothing requirement, and a project declaring no labels block at all behaves identically to before this mechanism existed.

Validation:

  • Completeness is a hard-fail. Every declared label must carry a translation for every declared site language — mirrors the chrome-string completeness rule (DiagnosticKind::IncompleteLabelTranslation).
  • Data-existence is advisory. A label naming a property/class absent from the project's data produces a non-gating Warning (DiagnosticKind::UnknownLabel) — it catches typos in a label's key without blocking boot, mirroring the sparse-property warning family.

Where it's used: facet-group headings, the resource-detail eyebrow (the class label above the title) and per-property <dt>-equivalent labels, and the resource-list surf-head class title. See the "Alice demo" cross-reference in CLAUDE.md's "New public surface (config-translatable-labels)" entry for the exact call sites.

E1's empty-class title fallback (empty-states-not-found plan). The resource-list surf-head's class-label title used to read empty on a genuinely-empty class — render_surf_head previously derived the label from list.items.first(), which doesn't exist when there are no items. It now resolves the label independently via resolve_class_label from the class the ir::Component::ResourceList carries, so the title (and the "0 resources" count line) render correctly even when the list is empty — the same labels { class } declaration that resolves the populated-branch eyebrow.

Optional plural child on class entries. A class entry may nest an optional plural { <lang> "…" } child holding the class's localized plural noun. This is a general class-noun declaration, not a search-bar-only knob — several separate engine surfaces resolve it:

labels {
    class "Character" {
        en "Character"
        de "Figur"
        plural {
            en "characters"
            de "Figuren"
        }
    }
}

The resolver is resolve_class_plural (areas/access/cpe/core/src/labels.rs) and its capitalizing wrapper resolve_class_plural_capitalized (same module). Its consumers:

  1. the narrowed-to-zero copy (search and facet no-match) — chrome::narrowed_to_zero_text's noun, via resolve_class_plural in SearchFragmentSurface::resolve (web/src/page.rs); used as declared.
  2. the browse breadcrumb / eyebrow — resolve_class_plural_capitalized (render_browse_breadcrumb_for_page, web/src/page.rs).
  3. the resource-detail class crumb — resolve_class_plural_capitalized (render_record_breadcrumb_for_page, web/src/page.rs).
  4. the 404 / not-found (N3) "browse all" exit — chrome::nf_browse_all_text(class_plural, lang), which render_not_found (areas/access/cpe/components/src/component/resource_detail.rs) hands the resolved plural, used as declared.
  5. the browse count line and its echo in the browse crumb's accessible name, and the dataset panel's count line — resolve_class_plural beside resolve_class_label (see the class-noun count line below); used as declared.
  6. the incoming-links caption when its label= does not resolve — resolve_class_plural_capitalized (web/src/page.rs).

Two nearby surfaces stay singular by engine design — don't "fix" either to the plural:

  • the not-found page's class crumb uses resolve_class_label (singular, render_record_breadcrumb_for_page's unresolved-id branch, web/src/page.rs); only the "browse all" exit beside it takes the plural.
  • render_surf_head's browse title uses resolve_class_label (component/resource_list.rs), so /books reads "Buch · 19 Bücher" — the TITLE is the singular; the count line beside it takes the plural (resolve_class_plural) and, at one result, the singular (see the class-noun count line below).

Practical consequence for how you spell the declared value: the crumbs and the incoming-links caption capitalize the resolved noun, and the sentence copy (no-match, browse-all, count lines) uses it as declared, so declare DE plurals capitalized ("Bücher", "Figuren") and EN plurals lowercase ("books", "characters") — the crumb capitalizes what it gets, the sentences don't. (German common nouns are always capitalized anyway; this is what makes the split work.)

The trap. An absent plural block is legal, so a declared class without one degrades three live surfaces (browse eyebrow, detail class crumb, 404 browse-all exit) to the capitalized singular — e.g. "Buch" and "Alle Buch durchsuchen". Boot validation flags it advisorily: DiagnosticKind::MissingClassPlural (Warning, check_class_plurals) fires once per declared class label with no plural block — every one of them, whether or not the class has a page bound to it. Declare plural for every declared class.

The bare <lang> "…" children remain the singular label (the eyebrow/ surf-head text) — unaffected by plural's presence. Resolution order (never panics; always returns a usable noun): the declared plural for the request language → the declared plural for the default/any language → the class's own singular label (resolve_class_label, itself falling back to humanize_property_name). This is a deliberate reuse of the EXISTING labels { class } mechanism rather than a second, parallel class-noun source (e.g. a search-bar label="…" chrome attr) — keep the singular and plural forms declared together in one place. Completeness applies to a declared plural block exactly like the singular labels: every site language must have a plural translation once the block exists at all (hard-fail, reusing DiagnosticKind::IncompleteLabelTranslation); an ABSENT plural block is not a violation — it just falls through to the singular/humanized fallback chain above.

remodel block

The remodel mapping: the part of a project's re-modelling that is declared and not coded. It says how the store builder turns the project's archive snapshot into CPE's store: which archive classes and properties become which CPE ones, how a resource gets its id and its image, which class is a member of which, the list vocabularies, the shortcode, the text the archive's editors wrote where a value was not known, how the images are served, and which classes annotations may touch. What a project needs and the block cannot say is code, the project's hook; the block says that there is one and what it may do (the hook node, under "The hook"). The block is the store builder's (areas/access/cpe/store-build/README.md) input: the builder lowers it through cpe_core::validate::load_remodel and builds the project's store from the archive snapshot, the block and, where the block declares one, the hook. Here the builder runs at the project's Activation, called by cpe-server; the page assembly validates the block with the rest of the file and does not use it. For where Incunabula's data comes from, see areas/access/cpe/projects/incunabula/PROVENANCE.md.

The block is optional and top-level, at most once (see "Top-level structure"). A node or attribute that the grammar below does not list is refused as unknown. The worked example is Incunabula's block: the remodel node stands in projects/incunabula/config.kdl as written here, line for line, IRIs in full. A test of the store builder (areas/access/cpe/store-build/tests/it/worked_example.rs) lowers the example and the file and holds the two equal.

site {
    title "Incunabula"
    languages "de" "en"
}

remodel {
    shortcode "0803"
    sentinel "[missing]"
    hook {
        key "sort_key" class="Book"
        key "catalogue_uri" class="Book"
        key "catalogue_uri_replaces" class="Book"
        provides "sort-key" class="Book"
        provides "side" class="BorderStrip"
        overrides "catalogue-uri" class="Book"
        drops class="Page"
    }

    list "office" {
        list-node "amerbach" { de "Johann Amerbach"; en "Johann Amerbach" }
        list-node "bergmann" { de "Johann Bergmann de Olpe"; en "Johann Bergmann de Olpe" }
        list-node "furter" { de "Michael Furter"; en "Michael Furter" }
        list-node "ysenhut" { de "Lienhart Ysenhut"; en "Lienhart Ysenhut" }
        list-node "other" { de "Richel · Wolff · ohne genannten Drucker"; en "Richel · Wolff · unnamed printer" }
    }
    list "side" {
        list-node "left" { de "links"; en "left" }
        list-node "right" { de "rechts"; en "right" }
    }

    class "Book" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#Book" no-addresses=#true {
        id curated-key="slug"
        property "name" from="label" curated-key="title_override"
        property "alt-title" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasTitle" type="text" exclude-label=#true
        property "creator" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasCreator" type="text"
        property "publisher" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasPublisher" type="text"
        property "pub-place" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasPubloc" type="text" max=1 sentinel="absent"
        property "shelfmark" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasLocation" type="text" max=1
        property "physical" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasPhysicalDesc" type="text" max=1
        property "catalogue-uri" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasUri" type="uri" max=1
        property "pub-date" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasPubdate" type="date" min=1 max=1 display-key="date_display"
        curated "office" key="office" type="list" list="office" min=1
        curated "teaser" key="teaser" type="per-language"
        member-count "extent" of="Page"
        cover curated-key="cover_page"
    }
    images class="Image" iiif-base="https://iiif.dasch.swiss/0803/" {
        authorship "Universitätsbibliothek Basel"
        license "CC BY 4.0"
    }
    class "Page" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#Page" image=#true {
        member-of "Book" seq="seq-number"
        id from="property" property="name" under-parent=#true
        property "name" "page-id" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasPagenum" type="text" min=1 max=1 empty="refuse" sentinel="keep"
        property "description" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasDescription" type="text" max=1
        property "comment" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasComment" type="text"
        property "strip-left" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasBandTypeL" type="link" max=1 target="BorderStrip"
        property "strip-right" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasBandTypeR" type="link" max=1 target="BorderStrip"
    }
    class "BorderStrip" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#Band" image=#true {
        id curated-key="slug" from="label"
        property "name" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasTitle" type="text" curated-key="name" min=1 max=1 empty="refuse" sentinel-within="keep"
        property "description" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasDescription" type="text" max=1 sentinel="absent" sentinel-within="keep"
        property "comment" iri="http://www.knora.org/ontology/0803/incunabula#hasComment" type="text" empty="refuse" sentinel-within="keep"
        incoming-count "page-uses" from="Page" {
            via "strip-left"
            via "strip-right"
        }
    }

    annotations {
        on "Page"
        link-targets "Book" "Page"
    }
}

Grammar

Every node not listed, at any depth, is UnknownChildNode, except below a list-node: there every child is read as a language label, and one in a language the site does not declare is UnknownRemodelReference (a label with an attribute or a child of its own is still UnknownRemodelAttribute or UnknownChildNode). Every attribute not listed is UnknownRemodelAttribute. A required attribute that is absent is MissingRequiredAttribute and a wrong-typed one is InvalidAttributeType. A required node or argument that is absent is MissingRequiredAttribute too, located at the parent (or, for an argument, at the node). A node that occurs more often than its count allows is DuplicateRemodelEntry, located at the extra node, and so is an attribute written twice on one node, located at that node. A node takes exactly the arguments the table lists: a further positional argument, or any on a node listed with none, is InvalidRemodelValue. A text that must name something (a class, property, curated, count or list name, a list-node name, a slug, a label, an iri, a curated-key, display-key or target, a curated node's key= or list=, an id's property=, a member-of parent or seq=, an of=, an incoming-count's from=, a via, the images class=, authorship, license, a class name of on or link-targets, the argument and the class= of a hook child) is InvalidRemodelValue when empty. "n" is how often a node may occur in its parent. Every diagnostic is an error.

NodenArguments and attributes (required unless a default is given)Errors beyond the general ones
remodel0..1, top levelnonea second block is UnexpectedTopLevelNode
shortcode1one stringInvalidRemodelValue unless four characters of 0-9A-F
sentinel0..1one stringInvalidRemodelValue when empty, and when it starts or ends with whitespace (a text is compared with it stripped, so such a sentinel would match none)
hook0..1no argument; children key, provides, overrides and drops, each 0..nDuplicateRemodelEntry for a second hook; InvalidRemodelValue for an argument
hook › key0..na curated key; class=UnknownRemodelReference for a class= no class declares; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a key that class already declares
hook › provides0..na CPE property name; class=UnknownRemodelReference for a class= no class declares; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a name that class already has; ReservedRemodelName for image in a block with an images node
hook › overrides0..na CPE property name; class=UnknownRemodelReference for a class= no class declares, and for a name no property node of that class has; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a property two overrides nodes name, under one of its names or under two
hook › drops0..nno argument; class=UnknownRemodelReference for a class= no class declares; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a class two drops nodes name; ConflictingRemodelAttributes for a class that another class is member-of
list0..nthe list's nameDuplicateRemodelEntry for a name declared twice
list › list-node1..nthe node's slug; one child per site language, named by the language, holding the labelDuplicateRemodelEntry for a slug twice in one list and for a language twice in one node; IncompleteListTranslation for a site language without a label; UnknownRemodelReference for a label language the site does not declare
class1..nthe class's CPE name; iri=; image=#true (default #false); no-addresses=#true (default #false)DuplicateRemodelEntry for a name or an iri declared twice; ReservedRemodelName for the name the images block gives its class=; ConflictingRemodelAttributes for image in a block without an images node
id1 per classno argument; curated-key= (optional); from="label"|"property"|"iri" (optional); property= (with from="property"); under-parent=#true (default #false)ConflictingRemodelAttributes for neither curated-key nor from, for property without from="property" and for from="property" without property, and for under-parent on a class without a member-of or beside curated-key; UnknownRemodelReference for a property that names no text property of the class with max=1; InvalidRemodelValue for a from outside its three words; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a curated key the class already declares
member-of0..1 per classthe parent class's name; seq= (optional, a CPE property name)UnknownRemodelReference for a parent no class declares; RemodelMembershipCycle for the class itself or a longer cycle; DuplicateRemodelEntry and ReservedRemodelName for the seq name as for any property name
property0..n per classone or more CPE names; a source, either iri= with type="text"|"uri"|"date"|"link" or from="label"; curated-key=; min= (default 0); max= (default none); empty="drop"|"refuse" (default "drop"); sentinel="refuse"|"absent"|"keep" (default "refuse"); sentinel-within="refuse"|"keep" (default "refuse"); exclude-label=#true; display-key=; target=ConflictingRemodelAttributes for both sources or none, for an iri without a type, for a link without a target, for an attribute the form does not take (the table below), for exclude-label beside curated-key and for sentinel or sentinel-within in a block without a sentinel node; DuplicateRemodelEntry for an iri another property of the class has, for a name the class already has and for a curated key the class already declares; UnsupportedRemodelType and UnknownRemodelType (below); InvalidRemodelValue for a max below the min, a min or max that is negative or above 4294967295, and a word outside the closed vocabulary of from, empty, sentinel or sentinel-within; UnknownRemodelReference for a target no class declares
curated0..n per classthe CPE name; key=; type="text"|"list"|"per-language"; list= (with type="list"); min= (0 or 1, default 0)MissingRequiredAttribute for an absent key= or type=; ConflictingRemodelAttributes for list= beside another type and for type="list" without list=; UnknownRemodelReference for a list= no list declares; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a name the class already has and for a curated key the class already declares; InvalidRemodelValue for a type outside its three words and for a min other than 0 or 1
member-count0..n per classthe CPE name; of=UnknownRemodelReference when of names no class, or a class that is not member-of this one; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a name the class already has
incoming-count0..n per classthe CPE name; from=; children via 1..n, each one CPE property name of the from classUnknownRemodelReference for a from no class declares and for a via that names no property of it; ConflictingRemodelAttributes for a via that names a property that is no link, or a link whose target is not this class; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a name the class already has and for a property two via nodes name
cover0..1 per classno argument; curated-key=MissingRequiredAttribute for an absent curated-key=; ConflictingRemodelAttributes in a block without an images node, on a class no class is member-of, and beside the class's image; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a curated key the class already declares
images0..1class= (the CPE name of the image class); iiif-base=; children authorship 1 and license 1, each one stringInvalidRemodelValue for a base that is not https://, a host and /
annotations0..1children on 0..1 and link-targets 0..1, each one or more class namesUnknownRemodelReference for a name no class declares; DuplicateRemodelEntry for a name repeated within one on or link-targets

Which property attribute goes with which of its five forms. An attribute that is present on a form that does not take it is ConflictingRemodelAttributes: presence decides, so exclude-label=#false on a uri is one too. type goes with the four iri forms and with from="label" never. Such an attribute is one mistake and is reported once: what it holds is not judged, so empty="x" on a uri, target="Ghost" on a text and sentinel="keep" on a date in a block without a sentinel node each give that one diagnostic. The same holds for a curated node's list= beside a type other than list, and for an id's property= without from="property".

Attributeiri textiri uriiri dateiri linkfrom="label"
curated-keyyesnononoyes
emptyyesnononono (an empty label is always refused)
min, maxyesyesyesyesno
sentinel, sentinel-within (need a sentinel node)yesyesnonono
exclude-label (not with curated-key)yesnononono
display-keynonoyesnono
targetnononorequiredno

Readings of the table, as built:

  • type. integer, decimal, boolean, list-node, geometry and color are UnsupportedRemodelType, a located "not supported yet". The type word list-node names the archive port's value kind and has nothing to do with the list-node node. Any other word is UnknownRemodelType.
  • A property's source. A property has either an iri with a type, or from="label". Both, or neither, is ConflictingRemodelAttributes, and so is an iri without a type and a type beside from="label". from takes the one word label; any other is InvalidRemodelValue. A property with a faulty source is still held to the table above, in the same pass: an attribute is reported when neither the form its type names nor, with from present, the label form takes it. Only a node that names no form at all (no from and no readable type) is not checked against the table.
  • References. A link's target, a member-of parent, a member-count's of and an incoming-count's from name a declared class, and a curated node's list= a declared list, each anywhere in the block: a class declared further down resolves. An id's property names a property of its own class and a via one of the from class, by any of the property's names, wherever in the class it stands. A name no node declares is UnknownRemodelReference. A link without a target is ConflictingRemodelAttributes.
  • Ids. Every class has exactly one id; a class without one is MissingRequiredAttribute, located at the class. An id has a curated-key, a from, or both: the key alone requires a curated value, and with a from beside it the from is what the id is made of when no value is curated. Neither is ConflictingRemodelAttributes. property goes with from="property" and with no other from, and from="property" needs it; a mismatch either way is ConflictingRemodelAttributes. The property names a text property of the class that holds at most one value (max=1); a name of no property, of a property of another type or of one without max=1 is UnknownRemodelReference. under-parent goes only on a class with a member-of, and not beside curated-key.
  • Membership. member-of names the class whose resources this class's resources are members of. A class that names itself, or whose parents' own member-of nodes lead back to it, is RemodelMembershipCycle, reported at each member-of on the cycle; a class that only leads into a cycle is not reported. seq= is the name of the property the member's position is stored under.
  • Member and incoming counts. A member-count's of names a class that is member-of the class the count stands on; any other class, the class itself among them, is UnknownRemodelReference. Each via of an incoming-count names a link property of the from class whose target is the class the count stands on; a property that is no link, or a link to another class, is ConflictingRemodelAttributes, located at the via. An incoming-count needs at least one via and names no property twice, under one of its names or under two; the from class may be the class itself.
  • A faulty node is reported once. A reference to a node that is itself refused is not reported a second time: an id or a via that names a property whose names, source (a type without an iri among them), max or target are faulty, and a member-count or cover on a class whose would-be member has a member-of that names no class, give no diagnostic of their own.
  • Images. image on a class and cover both need an images node in the block. A cover stands on a class that some class is member-of, and not beside image: a class takes its image from its own file or from a member, never both. Each mismatch is ConflictingRemodelAttributes, located at the class for image and at the cover otherwise.
  • Presence decides. As in the table above, a conflict is decided by an attribute being written, whatever its value: image=#false in a block without images, image=#false beside a cover and under-parent=#false on a class without a member-of are each ConflictingRemodelAttributes.
  • Counts. min defaults to 0 and max to none. A negative min or max, one above 4294967295 (the largest count the mapping holds), and a max below the min, are InvalidRemodelValue. A curated node's min is 0 or 1, and min=1 marks the value required; any other is InvalidRemodelValue.
  • Closed words. from, empty, sentinel, sentinel-within and a curated node's type take the words the table lists and no other; another is InvalidRemodelValue. The two type attributes differ here: a curated node's type word outside its three is InvalidRemodelValue, while a property's type word that is no value kind is UnknownRemodelType. sentinel= and sentinel-within= need a sentinel node in the block: without one they are ConflictingRemodelAttributes.
  • A curated node. key= and type= are required; either absent is MissingRequiredAttribute. list= goes with type="list" and with no other type, and type="list" needs it; a mismatch either way is ConflictingRemodelAttributes.
  • Names are per class. One namespace of CPE property names per class holds the name of every node that yields a property: its property nodes (each of their names), its curated, member-count and incoming-count nodes, its member-of's seq=, and each provides the hook node declares on the class. A name taken twice, also once by each of two kinds, is DuplicateRemodelEntry. Within one class no two property nodes share an iri. Two classes may use the same iri or the same property name. One property node with several names is the form for one source under two names.
  • A reserved name. In a block with an images node the property name image is taken: it names the link from a resource to its image, which is the mapping's own to write. Any node that takes it is ReservedRemodelName. A block without images may use the name.
  • Curated keys are per class. A curated key is declared wherever it is read: curated-key= of an id, a cover or a property, display-key= of a property, key= of a curated, and a key of the hook node, which is a key the hook reads on the class it names. A key declared twice on one class, in any two of these places, is DuplicateRemodelEntry; the same key on two classes is fine.
  • The hook node. Each child names a declared class, anywhere in the block, and the node itself may stand before or after the classes. A key and a provides are held against what their class declares, so a clash with a node of the class is reported at the hook's child. An overrides names a property node of its class by any of the property's names; a curated node or a count cannot be overridden, and a property is overridden once, whichever of its names the nodes use. A drops takes no argument, and a class is dropped from once.
  • list and class. A list needs at least one list-node, and the block needs at least one class. The lowering keeps the declared order of classes and of list nodes.
  • No site language. When the site declares no language, a list-node is not checked per language (no IncompleteListTranslation, no UnknownRemodelReference for a label) and its labels are kept as written. validate::load_remodel, the entry meant for the store builder, refuses such a site instead (MissingSiteLanguages).
