Every string in the catalog carries a doc comment noting whether it's a pre-existing draft (migrated verbatim from an already-4-language per-module helper that predated the catalog) or new (authored to fill a gap — settings.rs, the skip-link/cog-label, previously unbranched aria-labels, and the site index). Both kinds are unreviewed fr/it drafts pending native-speaker review; see docs/plans/chrome-localization/translations-to-review.md for the full review table.

"Complete" excludes proper nouns and brand/legal marks. A handful of literal strings are deliberately left as bare English constants, not ChromeMsg variants: the "CPE" wordmark, the "DSP APP" link label, the org's official name ("Swiss National Data and Service Center for the Humanities", both standalone and inside the © line), and the © line itself. These don't vary by language — they're proper nouns / legal text, not descriptive or navigational chrome — so routing them through the catalog would add four identical rows per string with no translation to review. "Complete" for this catalog means every language-varying descriptive and navigational engine string, not literally every string the engine's renderers emit.

Narrative language fallback (Phase 3.9)

A narrative file="home.md" component resolves its content via a 3-rung fallback chain, tried in order:

  1. <stem>.<requested-lang>.<ext> (e.g. home.fr.md) — the visitor's resolved request language.
  2. <stem>.<default-language>.<ext> (e.g. home.en.md) — skipped when the default language is itself the requested one (already tried at step 1).
  3. the base file as declared in config (e.g. home.md).

The first rung present in the narrative/ directory wins; title derivation (compose_page_title's narrative-heading path) uses the exact same chain, so a page's <title> and body content can never disagree on which variant was picked.

Per-language variant files are therefore optional — a project may add home.fr.md without also authoring home.de.md, and visitors requesting an un-authored language transparently see the default-language content instead of an empty page. Boot validation only guarantees the terminal rung of the chain is reachable: a narrative file must resolve to the base file or the default-language variant (NarrativeFileNotFound hard-fails otherwise) — because those are the two rungs the chain is guaranteed to reach. A bundle offering only a non-default variant (e.g. home.fr.md with no home.md and no home.en.md, en being the default) fails at boot rather than silently rendering an empty article for every visitor who doesn't request fr.

Validation surface (boot-time)

Per cpe-poc.md §11 and re-stated here for the config view. This is the full v1 validation target. Data-dependent checks marked below require the query layer; the Phase 2 boot validator performs only the config-internal checks. Phase 3 task two implemented the resource-detail-relevant subset; the rest land in Phase 5. See the "Validation" section of dsp-incubator cpe/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

  • KDL syntax parses cleanly.
  • Every top-level node is site, labels, page or remodel. Other top-level nodes hard-fail (UnexpectedTopLevelNode), and so does a second remodel.
  • The site block has the required attributes (title, languages).
  • Every page has unique id and route (within the project).
  • Every component node is one of the v1 components (or a project-registered custom component — the (project, name) registry in areas/access/cpe/core/src/validate/project_components.rs; timeline is the first tenant, and woodcut-cases, edition-cards and strip-row followed in Slice 7, see "timeline" and "woodcut-cases, edition-cards, strip-row" above and dsp-incubator cpe/docs/adr/0011-per-project-components.md). Unknown component → hard-fail.
  • Every component's required attributes are present and have the right value shape.
  • Component references (target, source) resolve.
  • A literal-id resource-detail references a resource that exists in the data (hard-fail). (Phase 3 task two — implemented.)
  • Property names in show-properties and title-property on a resource-detail exist on the resource's class (warn — sparse data is OK). (Phase 3 task two — implemented.) Property names named by a group are covered by the same sparse check (a shared detail_property_names helper flattens show-properties + every group's members + title-property into one list — Incunabula Slice 3 / G8).
  • A property named by more than one group, or by a group and show-properties, is DuplicateGroupedProperty (hard-fail) — one diagnostic per repeated name; a repeat within one group alone, or within show-properties alone, is out of scope. A group label= that is not a declared chrome { string } id is UnknownGroupLabel (warning — falls back to the built-in caption). A group empty= that is not a declared chrome id is UnknownGroupEmptyLabel (warning — the group renders as if empty= were unset); a non-string empty= is InvalidAttributeType. (Incunabula Slice 3 / G8 — implemented; empty= HdM Slice 3.)
  • Two narrative-for entries on one resource-detail naming the same resource id is DuplicateNarrativeFor (hard-fail). A narrative-for file= runs the same InvalidNarrativePath/NarrativeFileNotFound checks (hard-fail) a page-level narrative node's file does. A narrative-for resource id absent from the data is UnknownNarrativeForResource (warning — the intro just never attaches). (Incunabula Slice 3 / O6 — implemented.) There is no dedicated positional-argument DiagnosticKind — the first positional string (the resource id) reuses MissingRequiredAttribute (absent) and InvalidAttributeType (present but non-string), same as any other required attribute; the diagnostic message names "first positional argument (a resource id)" so it's still distinguishable from a real attribute failure.
  • Two parameterised resource-detail pages binding the same class value produce AmbiguousClassRoute (hard-fail). (Phase 5 — implemented.)
  • A link value's target_id that does not exist in the data produces UnknownLinkTarget (warning — the renderer degrades gracefully to span.unresolved). The check is best-effort over boot-reachable resources; $param pages cannot be pre-walked. (Phase 5 — implemented.)
  • A compound-viewer with a literal source that has no compound_parts rows produces EmptyCompoundSource (warning — renders empty state, doesn't crash; $param sources are skipped). (Phase 5 — implemented.)
  • Property names referenced by where/sort for resource-list — hard-fail (UnknownResourceListProperty) if the property exists nowhere in the data at all; warn (SparseResourceListProperty) if it exists somewhere in the data but on no resource of this class. (Phase 5 — implemented.) The check is two-tier by presence, not by a coverage ratio: SparseResourceListProperty fires only when the property is present on no resource of the class at all (!class_props.contains(prop)); once it is present on even one, the check is silent regardless of how thin the coverage is — HdM's gloss property="genre-varieties" (present on 2,363 of 2,449 Works) and chip property="role" (1,221 of 1,222 People) fire no warning. Don't predict a sparse warning from a coverage percentage; predict it only from "does at least one resource of this class carry the property at all".
  • Property names referenced by searches for search-bar — hard-fail (UnknownSearchProperty) if the property exists nowhere in the data; hard-fail (IncompatibleSearchProperty) if its value_type on the target class is neither text nor richtext; warn (SparseSearchProperty) if it exists on some resources of the class but not all. q is a reserved query key (RESERVED_FACET_PROPERTIES) — a facet property named q also hard-fails. (search-bar plan — implemented.)
  • An optional plural { <lang> "…" } child under a labels { class } entry must carry every declared site language once present at all (hard-fail, reusing IncompleteLabelTranslation); an absent plural block is not a hard-fail — but it degrades the browse eyebrow, the detail class crumb and the 404 browse-all exit to the capitalized singular, so it warns (MissingClassPlural). (search-bar plan — implemented; the warning is the backlog quick-wins batch; see the labels block section above for all four consumers.)
  • A facet with a valid but non-list kind (e.g. date-decade, text, boolean, range, date-year) → hard-fail (UnsupportedFacetKind). (Phase 5 — implemented.)
  • Facet kind is compatible with the property's value type → hard-fail (IncompatibleFacetKind). A list-kind facet requires list_value rows on the target class. (Phase 5 — implemented for the list kind.)
  • Facet property absent from the data entirely → hard-fail (UnknownFacetProperty). (Phase 5 — implemented.)
  • Facet property exists in the data but not on the target class → warn (SparseFacetProperty). (Phase 5 — implemented.)
  • Route param references in $param substitutions match declared params.
  • Nav route values exist as declared page routes (hard-fail, UnresolvedNavRoute). (Phase 3.8 — implemented.)
  • The one-row desk header fits: for each declared language, the resolved site title, every resolved nav label, the language summary (two or more languages) and the appearance box, with the desk form's gaps, must fit the 1,170px the 79rem desk breakpoint leaves (the 1264px window less two gutters; 1,280px at 100rem before the layout pass). An estimate over it warns (HeaderRowOverBudget { lang, estimated_px, budget_px }, one per language) — the title ellipsises there, so it is advisory. Text is estimated from per-face average advances calibrated for Newsreader and IBM Plex Mono; a project with another typeface gets the same constants, and the estimate holds for Latin-script text only. Config-internal, so both validation outcomes report it (when the site {} block itself lowers, like MissingClassPlural), and like every Warning it shows in the serve log, not in cpe --check. (general chrome — implemented; areas/access/cpe/core/src/validate/header_budget.rs.)
  • Narrative file references resolve to the base file or the default-language variant (hard-fail, NarrativeFileNotFound); other per-language variants are optional. (Phase 3.9 — implemented; see "Narrative language fallback" above.)
  • A resource-list with grid=#true and no media attribute → hard-fail (GridWithoutMedia). (grid-mode plan — implemented.)
  • A resource-list tile-ratio= outside the W:H grammar → hard-fail (InvalidAttributeType); with a valid ratio and no grid=#true → hard-fail (TileRatioWithoutGrid). (layout pass — implemented.)
  • site { narrative-companion | narrative-side | text-align } with a string outside its two values → hard-fail (UnknownSiteValue); companion= or side= on a narrative that is not its page's first → hard-fail (NarrativeLayoutNotFirst). (layout pass — implemented.)
  • Two narratives of one page with the same authored heading id, in the content one visitor is served → hard-fail (DuplicateHeadingIdOnPage). Data-dependent (it reads the narrative files), so it runs in both validate_with_data arms. (layout pass — implemented.)
  • A single page {} declaring both a compound-viewer and a paginating resource-list → hard-fail (CompoundViewerWithPagedList). Both read the ?page= query key — a member address (?page=<id|name|prefix>) vs. a page number (?page=N). "Paginating" means per-page, or no per-page/limit at all (the default is per-page 20); a resource-list with limit is compatible, and so is the pair on two different pages. Config-internal, so both validation outcomes report it. (Incunabula Slice 2 — implemented; see COMPONENT_LIBRARY.md's compound-viewer addressing contract.)
  • incoming-links (Incunabula Slice 5 / G7): more than one child on a resource-detail is DuplicateIncomingLinks (hard-fail); zero positional property args is IncomingLinksWithoutProperty (hard-fail) — both raised at lowering time (span-located, no page field). A label= that is not a declared chrome { string } id is UnknownIncomingLinksLabel (warning — falls back to the source class's capitalised plural). Three data-dependent checks, all in both validate_with_data arms: class= naming a class absent from the data is UnknownIncomingLinksClass (hard-fail — a query input, like resource-list's class); a listed property absent from the data entirely is UnknownIncomingLinksProperty (hard-fail); a listed property present in the data but carried by no resource of the declared source class is SparseIncomingLinksProperty (warning — the list would always be empty for it); a listed property stored with a value_type other than link is IncomingLinksPropertyNotLink (hard-fail — only link rows carry a target_id to reverse-resolve). (Incunabula Slice 5 / G7 — implemented.)
  • Grouped incoming-links (HdM Slice 3 / G3): group-by=, layout=, note-label=, row-label=, row-aside= and sort-property= are read with the reporting reader, so a present-but-wrong-typed value is InvalidAttributeType, and so is a layout= outside cards/columns. layout=/note-label= without group-by= are ignored (no diagnostic). A note-label= that is not a declared chrome { string } id is UnknownIncomingLinksNoteLabel (warning — the note is omitted); a declared one whose text lacks {n} in some language is IncomingLinksTextMissingPlaceholder (hard-fail, one per language). Both are config-internal. Three data-dependent checks, both arms, on each of row-label/row-aside/sort-property and a property group-by (the reserved group-by="via" names none): absent from the data or from every resource of the source class is UnknownIncomingLinksRowProperty (hard-fail); stored with the wrong type (group-by/row-aside need list_value or text, row-label/sort-property need text) is IncomingLinksRowPropertyWrongType (hard-fail); missing on some source resource that links through the declared properties is SparseIncomingLinksRowProperty (warning — those rows fall back). Each kind's attribute field names the attribute. With group-by= and no limit=, the limit is GROUPED_INCOMING_LIMIT_CEILING (1000), not 50. Group-key rules (ir::GroupKey, filled by query::incoming_links, so the renderer groups by plain equality): a text key keeps the stored spelling (never lowercased, so the group head reads as authored); case variants are folded in Rust (to_lowercase) onto the FIRST spelling met in row order. A list key is { key, label, seq }; a node with no list_nodes row sorts last (seq: i64::MAX) and its label falls back to the node id. group-by="via" and ungrouped specs always carry group: None (the renderer groups via by IncomingLink::via). List-valued labels (row-aside, group head) resolve requested lang → MIN(label), with NO "universal" rung — list_node_labels.lang is NOT NULL, so no language-less label exists (same rule as get_list_node_label); only text values use lang → universal → any. (HdM Slice 3 — implemented.)
  • Backlog hardening batch 3 (engine-hygiene-3): a resource-detail child node outside show-properties/group/narrative-for/ incoming-links is UnknownChildNode (hard-fail, config-internal — see "resource-detail's recognised child nodes" above); a resource-detail class="…" naming a class absent from the data is UnknownResourceDetailClass (hard-fail, data-dependent, both arms — see the class attribute section above); an incoming-links property that is link-typed, present on its declared source class, and resolves to at least one target class, but never resolves to the page's own host class, is IncomingLinksPropertyMissesHost (warning, data-dependent, both arms — the list it drives will always be empty on this page). Also from this batch: ConflictingMediaProperty's fields are named registered_property/declared_property (not detail_property/ list_property — a compound-viewer registration is neither a "detail" nor a "list"; see the media section above for the full detail→compound→list registration order); and every optional string attribute in a lower_* fn now reports a present-but-wrong-typed value as InvalidAttributeType (resource-detail's id/title-property/ class/media, resource-list's id/media, compound-viewer's media/picker, search-bar's placeholder/scope, sort's direction) — previously these degraded silently to "absent", the way get_bool_attr never did for grid=. (engine-hygiene-3 — implemented.)
  • order-by (Incunabula Slice 8 / G9) on a resource-list: an absent key/property/label is MissingRequiredAttribute, a wrong-typed one (or a direction outside asc/desc) InvalidAttributeType; a key outside [a-z0-9-]+ is InvalidOrderKey, a built-in key (default/ name/name-desc/class/id) ReservedOrderKey, a repeated key within one list DuplicateOrderKey — all hard-fails raised at lowering time (span-located, no page field). A label= that is not a declared chrome { string } id is UnknownOrderLabel (hard-fail, config-internal, checked before the data fork). The option's property joins the where/sort two-tier check above in both validate_with_data arms. (Incunabula Slice 8 step 4 — implemented.)
  • order-default-label/order-name-property on a resource-list: a wrong-typed value is InvalidAttributeType; order-default-label is otherwise not boot-checked (an unresolvable id falls back to "As curated"), and order-name-property joins the where/sort two-tier check in both arms. (Incunabula books browse — implemented.)
  • The composed gloss { part …; teaser … } on a resource-list: a child other than part/teaser is UnknownChildNode { component: "gloss" }; property= plus children, no part, a second teaser, a repeated part property or a wrong-typed unit is InvalidAttributeType (all at lowering time). A unit= that is not a declared chrome string id is UnknownGlossUnit, and a unit translation without {n} is GlossUnitMissingPlaceholder (one per language) — both hard-fails, config-internal, checked before the data fork. A part stored as list_value/link/boolean, a teaser not stored as text/richtext, or unit= on a part not stored as integer/decimal is IncompatibleGlossPart (hard-fail, data-dependent, both arms). Every part and teaser property joins the where/sort two-tier check. (Incunabula books browse — implemented.)
  • Record header slots (book-page redesign): alt-title-property/ author-property wrong-typed is InvalidAttributeType; a child of imprint other than part is UnknownChildNode { component: "imprint" } and an empty imprint {} is an error (both config-internal); a slot property absent from the class is SparseProperty (Warning); a slot whose property holds a type it cannot render is IncompatibleGlossPart with the role alt-title, author or imprint part (hard-fail, data-dependent, both arms). IncompatibleGlossPart's message names the slot it concerns.
  • compound-viewer picker=: an unknown value or wrong type is InvalidAttributeType; picker on layout="contents" is PagesLayoutOnly (feature: "picker"; hard-fail, config-internal, before the data fork). member-links on layout="contents" is PagesLayoutOnly (feature: "member-links", same tier); its other checks: see its section above.
  • compound-viewer annotations= (Incunabula Slice 6): a non-boolean value is InvalidAttributeType; annotations=#true on layout="contents" is PagesLayoutOnly (feature: "annotations"; hard-fail, config-internal, before the data fork, so no -raw fixture).
  • group links-label= (Incunabula Slice 6): a non-string value is InvalidAttributeType; an id that is not a declared chrome { string } id is UnknownGroupLinksLabel (warning — the row falls back to ChromeMsg::AnnoRelated, "Verwandt" / "Related"). Config-internal, checked beside UnknownGroupLabel.
  • Annotation rows (Incunabula Slice 6, dsp-incubator cpe/docs/adr/0014-annotations-are-a-first-class-engine-store.md): every annotations and annotation_links row is checked against the rules the DDL does not enforce (SCHEMA.md §"Constraints not enforced in DDL"): a box inside the image (0..1, with a 1e-9 tolerance) with w and h above 0; a polygon must have points, and they must parse as whitespace-separated x,y pairs, at least three, each inside the box; no points on a rectangle or circle; a known shape; a colour, when present, as lowercase #rrggbb; a link with at least one target. One MalformedAnnotation (hard-fail) per broken rule. Data, not config, so both validate_with_data arms run it (one shared check_malformed_annotations); a failing query is InternalQueryError. Only a project whose data.sql carries annotation rows can trip it, which today is Incunabula alone.
  • site { not-found { browse } } (Incunabula Slice 8 / G11): a route that is not a declared page route is UnresolvedNotFoundBrowseRoute, and more than three browse entries is TooManyNotFoundBrowseLinks. Both are hard-fails and config-internal. (Incunabula Slice 8 step 7 — implemented.)
  • timeline (Incunabula Slice 4, the per-project custom component — see "timeline" above): class/date-property/lane-property absent, or any attribute wrong-typed, is MissingRequiredAttribute/ InvalidAttributeType (config-internal, span-located). An axis-start/ axis-end integer out of i32 range is TimelineAxisOutOfRange; an axis with axis-end <= axis-start or a span under three years is InvalidTimelineAxis (both config-internal). Three data-dependent checks, all in both validate_with_data arms: class naming a Class absent from the data is UnknownTimelineClass (hard-fail — a query input); date-property/lane-property/extent-property absent from the data entirely is UnknownTimelineProperty (hard-fail); a property stored with the wrong value_type for its role is IncompatibleTimelineProperty (hard-fail). date-property/ lane-property present in the data but carried by no resource of class is MissingTimelineProperty — a hard-fail, not the usual sparse-warn tier, since a timeline with no dated or no laned markers would render nothing useful; extent-property in the same situation is the ordinary SparseTimelineProperty (warning — the extent segment is just omitted). (Incunabula Slice 4 — implemented.)
  • Figure blocks and the three showcase components (Incunabula Slice 7, see their two sections above; the table there is the one list of their diagnostics): the slot's section, heading-id, more-route and label checks, the showcase grammar and label checks, and the data checks that keep every copied string verbatim. All are hard-fails. The narrative-content and data checks run in both validate_with_data arms, each pinned by a both-arms test. (Incunabula Slice 7 — implemented.)
  • The remodel block (see "remodel block" above; the grammar table there has each node's errors). Every kind below is a hard-fail, located at the offending node (MissingRemodelBlock has no location), and the block is lowered in one pass, so one boot reports every defect of it. An error in the block fails boot like an error in any other block, although the web binary does not use the mapping: it validates the whole file. Config-internal, so both validation outcomes report it. A second remodel block is UnexpectedTopLevelNode, the kind of every stray top-level node, at boot and in load_remodel alike. (per-project remodelling — implemented.)
    • MissingRemodelBlock — the config has no remodel block. Raised only by cpe_core::validate::load_remodel (the entry meant for the store builder), never at the web binary's boot: the block is optional there.
    • DuplicateRemodelEntry — a node occurs more often than its count allows; an attribute is written twice on one node; a list name, a list-node slug within its list, a label language within a node, a class name or a class iri is declared twice; a property repeats an iri its class already has; a property, a curated, a member-count, an incoming-count or a member-of seq= takes a CPE name its class already has, also from a node of another kind; a curated key (curated-key= of an id, a cover or a property, display-key=, key=, or a key of the hook node) is declared twice on one class; a provides of the hook node takes a name its class already has; two drops name one class; two overrides name one property; an on or link-targets names a class twice; two via nodes of one incoming-count name one property; a class has a second id, member-of or cover; the block has a second hook.
    • ReservedRemodelName — a class is named like the images block's class=; in a block with an images node, a property is named image.
    • UnknownRemodelAttribute — an attribute outside those the node takes.
    • UnknownRemodelType — a property type that is neither supported nor one of the six unsupported words.
    • UnsupportedRemodelType — a property type of integer, decimal, boolean, list-node, geometry or color.
    • InvalidRemodelValue — a shortcode that is not four characters of 0-9A-F, a sentinel that is empty or starts or ends with whitespace, or an iiif-base that is not https://, a host and /; an empty name (a class name of on or link-targets among them), slug, label, iri, curated-key, display-key, target, key=, list=, authorship or license; a positional argument beyond the one a node takes, or any on remodel, hook, drops, images, annotations, id or cover; an empty argument or class= of a hook child; a property max below its min, a min or max that is negative or above 4294967295, or a word outside the closed vocabulary of its from, empty, sentinel or sentinel-within; a curated type outside text, list and per-language, or a curated min other than 0 or 1; an id from outside label, property and iri; an empty property=, seq=, of=, from= of an incoming-count, via or member-of parent.
    • IncompleteListTranslation — a list-node without a label in a language the site declares.
    • UnknownRemodelReference — a list-node label in a language the site does not declare, a class name in annotations that no class declares, a property target that names no class, or a curated list= that names no list; a member-of parent or an incoming-count from= that names no class; a member-count of= that names no class that is member-of this one; an id property= that names no text property of its class with max=1; a via that names no property of the from class; a class= of a hook child that names no class, or an overrides that names no property node of its class.
    • ConflictingRemodelAttributes — a property with both an iri and a from, or with neither; with an iri and no type; a link without a target; an attribute its form does not take (including a type beside from="label"); exclude-label beside curated-key; sentinel or sentinel-within in a block without a sentinel node. A curated with list= beside a type other than list, or with type="list" and no list=. An id with neither a curated-key nor a from; with property and no from="property", or the reverse; with under-parent on a class without a member-of, or beside curated-key. A class image or a cover in a block without an images node; a cover on a class no class is member-of, or beside its class's image. A via that names a property that is no link, or a link whose target is another class. A drops of the hook node that names a class another class is member-of.
    • RemodelMembershipCycle — a member-of names its own class, or following the parents' own member-of nodes leads back to it; reported at each member-of on the cycle.
    • MissingRequiredAttribute — beyond an absent required attribute, argument or node anywhere in the block: a class without an id, a cover without curated-key=, an incoming-count without a via.
  • Chrome translations are complete.

Reporting: all errors printed in one pass at boot, with file path and line/column where KDL provides them. Boot exits non-zero on any hard-fail. A --check flag runs the validation and exits without starting the server, suitable for CI.

Authoring tips

(Captured here as the v1 audience is developer-authors; this is not a user-facing guide.)

  • Start by copying an existing project's config.kdl and editing.
  • Use cpe --check --project=<name> during edits to surface validation errors without booting the server.
  • narrative is the fastest place to iterate — Markdown files reload on each request (TBD — see cpe-poc.md §17 "Hot reload").
  • KDL doesn't enforce indentation. Two-space indents are the convention; the engine's --format flag (if added) will enforce it.

Out of scope for v1

  • Reusable templates / partials — repetition is acceptable. Reintroduce if it gets painful (cpe-poc.md §8.4.8).
  • Expressions and conditionals — KDL is declarative; computed values are out of scope. If a project needs computed binding, it uses the custom-component escape hatch.
  • Per-page CSS — all CSS comes from the token-CSS system at <base>/<project-id>/_static/cpe/*.css. No style="..." inline declarations in config. Per-project theming uses the theme {} knob; a style.css override is possible but deferred (see BACKLOG).
  • Per-component layout primitives — CSS handles layout; the config language doesn't have a grid or flex vocabulary.

CPE Operations

CPE has no image and no process of its own. The Access Area's binary, access-server, serves it beside DPE, and the image is the one DPE Operations describes. This page holds what is specific to CPE.

What is served

  • Where: every path under /cpe (CPE_BASE). A project is at /cpe/<project id>/; today there is one, Incunabula, at /cpe/incunabula/. /cpe and /cpe/ are CPE's overview: the projects it serves, each with a link to its start page. Any other path that names no project is CPE's own not-found page.
  • From what: the project folders in CPE_PROJECTS_DIR (configuration, narrative, assets) and sync's data in SYNC_DATA_DIR. Both are in the image. Each project's store is built in memory from that data at every start; nothing is written to disk, and a restart leaves nothing behind.
  • Static files: CPE's stylesheets, scripts and logos are compiled into the binary and served at /cpe/<project id>/_static/…, and at /cpe/_static/… for the overview and CPE's not-found page; a project's own files at /cpe/<project id>/_assets/….

Configuration

The four variables (CPE_BASE, CPE_PROJECTS_DIR, CPE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, SYNC_DATA_DIR) are in the environment table of DPE Operations. The image sets all but CPE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN. The three CPE_* values can also come from a cpe.toml in the working directory; the environment wins.

Start-up, and what CPE answers when something is missing

The port is bound first, and CPE's projects are loaded afterwards, in the background. Until they are, every path under /cpe answers 503 with Retry-After: 30 and Cache-Control: no-store. DPE and /healthz answer throughout. Nothing of CPE's stops the binary or delays its start.

/healthz says nothing about CPE. Whether Incunabula is served is read from the log line CPE's projects are loaded (served, unavailable) or from the status of /cpe/incunabula/.

A CPE request is traced by the binary's layers, under DPE's telemetry identity, with a span named by CPE's route (GET /cpe/incunabula/books/{id}).

Measurements

Measured on 2026-10-12. Two set-ups, both with the image's environment and the committed data (Incunabula: 4,198 resources, 20.3 MB in SYNC_DATA_DIR):

  • The image, built from a staged context as CI builds it, but for linux/arm64 (CI builds linux/amd64): a static musl binary, run with docker run --cpus=1 --memory=512m, the limits of a PR preview, under Docker Desktop on an Apple M5 Max.
  • The host: the release binary run on macOS on the same machine, from a directory laid out as the image.
The image, 1 CPU, 512 MiBThe image, 2 CPUs, 1 GiBThe host
Port bound, after process start0.06 to 0.07 s0.08 s0.21 s
Incunabula loaded, after process start1.12 to 1.14 s0.86 s0.63 to 0.64 s
of which loading the project1.05 to 1.08 s0.79 s0.42 to 0.43 s
Peak resident memory, start-up213 to 214 MiB213 MiB265 to 269 MiB
Resident memory once loaded136 MiB136 MiBnot read
Peak resident memory with CPE_BASE empty (DPE alone)154 MiBnot run173 to 194 MiB
Peak resident memory after 61,064 requests212 MiBnot run272 MiB

/healthz answered 200 before the log line CPE's projects are loaded in every run, and the first request to /cpe/incunabula/ answered 503. The memory figures are of the whole process, DPE included: the peak is reached while the project is loaded, and the snapshot, the built rows and the SQL text are freed afterwards. The 61,064 requests are a crawl of every URL Incunabula's pages link to, 48 at a time against the image and 8 against the host; after it Docker reported the container healthy, with no restart and no out-of-memory kill.

A PR preview on Cloud Run is deployed with --no-cpu-throttling. With throttling, an instance gets CPU only while it handles a request, and /cpe/incunabula/ answered 503 after a cold start until the sixth request. The load time on Cloud Run without throttling is not measured.

The image's data grew by 195,708 bytes (23 files, cpe/projects): the staged directory without the binary was 69,819,957 bytes before and is 70,015,665 bytes with it. sync/data (20,281,022 bytes) was already staged.

Response times: the baseline for store reads on the request path

A page's store reads run on the async worker threads the binary shares with DPE, and one project's requests wait on one lock (ARCH-MAP.md, areas/access/cpe). These figures are what a change to that is compared with. Times are to the last byte.

Every URL Incunabula's pages link to (61,064) was asked once by one client, on the host: median 1.0 ms, 95th percentile 1.9 ms, 99th 2.1 ms, slowest 9.5 ms. The slowest pages of that pass and five ordinary ones (18 pages) were then asked thirty times each by one client, and by eight clients at once, each its own process, 25 rounds over the list:

Incunabula has no search bar. A project with one has a request these figures do not cover.

Tests that start the binary

DPE's Playwright suites (end-to-end and accessibility) start access-server without CPE_BASE, so CPE is not mounted in them. just run and just dev set CPE_BASE=/cpe.

Editor Architecture

The metadata editor is the Deposit Area's first capability (ADR-0002, ADR-0003): the surface where a depositing project team edits its project metadata, RDU reviews it field by field, and an approved record is carried back into this repository as a pull request. Git stays the source of truth and the editor's database is working state (areas/deposit/ADR-0001).

This page describes the architecture as implemented. The Deposit Area's target lives only in its decision records, areas/deposit/docs/adr/, and the code matches them today; a gap that opens gets a "Divergence from the target architecture" section at the end of this page again (areas/deposit/editor/CLAUDE.md). Subsystem detail is on the topic pages each section links to.

The flow, end to end

flowchart LR
  D[Depositor] -->|edits, section by section| Draft
  Draft -->|submit| Sub[Submission]
  Sub -->|RDU decides each changed field| Round[Review round]
  Round -->|approve, one transaction| AR[Approved record]
  AR -->|GET /api/v1/approved-records| C[editor-pull-requests<br/>in GitHub Actions]
  C -->|one pull request per project| PR[Pull request on<br/>this repository]
  PR -->|CI checks, human merge, release| Corpus[Published project files]
  Corpus -->|baked into the image| DPE
  Corpus -->|baked into the image| E[editor, next deployment]
  E -->|reconcile at startup| Online
  • A Draft is the depositor's working copy: the project's JSON members verbatim, one per project, last write wins (The Project Representation, areas/deposit/ADR-0002).
  • A Submission is the draft as submitted, at most one per project. RDU claims it, decides each changed field, substitutes values beside the payload rather than over it, and ends the round with approve, request changes or reject; the depositor can withdraw (The Review Surface).
  • Approve writes the Approved record, the submitted draft with every decision applied, deletes the submission and appends the Review round, all in one transaction. The record waits for the pull-request run.
  • The pull-request run runs in GitHub Actions, never in the service. It reads every approved record over the editor's API, writes each project's onto an editor/<shortcode> branch, and opens or updates one pull request per project (Publishing to Git). Nothing is reported back. The pull request, its CI checks and a human merge are the gate between the editor and anything served.
  • Online is never stored. The merged file is baked into the next editor image, and the editor compares its records with that published set once at startup: a record whose data is published is discarded, and the project reads Online (Project State and Online Detection, areas/deposit/ADR-0003).

Components and crates

CrateFolderRole
editor-coreareas/deposit/editor/coreThe domain: the draft, the review diff, project state, the canonical project and entity writers, the published set, and one repository port per aggregate (no Axum, Maud or database dependency)
deposit-shellareas/deposit/shellThe area's document shell: page, the header and footer, the 403, 404 and problem pages, the sign-in link (safe_next, login_url) and the RDU-only text; depends on maud and mosaic-tiles only
identity-coreareas/deposit/identity/coreIdentity's domain: User, Role, Session, LoginCode, the login and session rules, code and token generation, the cookie names, the Mailer trait, and one repository port per aggregate with their IdentityRepositories bundle (no Axum, Maud or database dependency, and no editor-* dependency)
identity-portsareas/deposit/identity/portsWhat identity asks of the editor: OpenWork (an account's open drafts and submissions) and its fake; std only
identity-storeareas/deposit/identity/storeIdentity's SQLite store, the file identity.sqlite: the tables behind identity's four repository ports, its migration and pool, the mail transports (SmtpMailer, ConsoleMailer) behind identity-core's Mailer, and the adapters LiveAuthenticator and LiveUserDirectory behind editor-ports
identity-webareas/deposit/identity/webIdentity's HTTP surface: the login and depositor pages, their handlers and route table, identity's own Authenticated/Rdu extractors and the Set-Cookie glue, and the Identity facade (start: the RDU accounts, the mailer and the hourly sweep; router)
editor-portsareas/deposit/editor/portsWhat the editor asks of identity: Actor, Authenticator, UserDirectory and their fakes; std only
editor-storeareas/deposit/editor/storeThe editor's SQLite store, the file editor.sqlite: the tables behind editor-core's five repository ports, its migration and pool, and the adapter LiveOpenWork behind identity-ports; no foreign keys
editor-webareas/deposit/editor/webThe editor's HTTP surface: the Maud views (pages, the form's field registry and widgets), the handlers and route table, the editor's Authenticated/Rdu extractors over Authenticator, the startup reconcile, and the Editor facade (start: the published set, the temporal tables, the agents and the reconcile; router)
deposit-serverareas/deposit/serverThe binary and composition root: configuration, observability, the CSRF and OTel layers, the untraced routes, the page-URL normalizer built from both web crates' route paths, and the fallback 404; opens the two stores, starts identity and then the editor, and merges their routers
editor-pull-requestsareas/deposit/editor/pull-requestsThe CI binary that turns approved records into pull requests (Publishing to Git)

Dependency direction is server → web → core. deposit-server depends on the two web crates (identity-web and editor-web, which it mounts through the Identity and Editor facades), the two store crates, the two ports crates and deposit-shell, and on no core crate, dev-dependencies included (.github/scripts/check-composition-root-deps.sh). identity-web depends on identity's own crates, deposit-shell, mosaic-tiles and shared-*; deposit-shell depends on no capability crate; identity-core depends on no editor crate; the two ports crates depend on std alone; the two store crates each depend on their own core crate and on the other capability's ports crate, the one it answers; editor-pull-requests sits outside that chain, depending on editor-core and shared-metadata alone and running as a batch job rather than serving a request. editor-web depends on editor-core for the project representation it renders and the repository ports it reads through, on editor-ports, deposit-shell, mosaic-tiles and shared-*, and on no identity crate. .github/scripts/check-capability-deps.sh (just check) holds the edges between capabilities, from a capability or the shell to anything outside its area, and from a ports crate to anything but shared-*, and it keeps third-party crates out of the ports crates, web frameworks, Maud and database crates out of the core crates, and web frameworks out of the shell; inside a capability it allows any workspace edge, and the root's edges are check-composition-root-deps.sh's. Component CSS is collected from the Tailwind entry's @source globs rather than from the crate graph, so it ships independently of that dependency (Rendering).

Unlike DPE, the HTML document shell is the area's, not a capability's: deposit-shell (areas/deposit/shell) holds the document, header and footer, the 403, 404 and problem pages, the sign-in link with the area's one open-redirect check (safe_next), and the RDU-only text, so identity's pages and the editor's share one copy without either depending on the other. It depends on no capability crate and has no Axum: editor-web's and identity-web's shell.rs each turn its markup into responses, and deposit-server's renders the fallback 404. The routes it links (/, /projects, /login, /logout) are string literals.

Inside deposit-server, serve.rs opens both stores, starts identity through identity_web::Identity::start and then the editor through editor_web::Editor::start, handing the editor identity-store's LiveAuthenticator and LiveUserDirectory; router.rs merges the two routers and owns the layer order (Routing). Inside editor-web, the handlers are one module per surface under handlers/ (sections, review, entities, projects, approved), and only they use Axum; EditorState holds editor: Arc<dyn EditorRepositories>, the editor store's implementation of editor-core's five repository ports (Persistence), and the two ports it asks identity through: the handlers authenticate through Authenticator (handlers/auth.rs) and read names through UserDirectory. reconcile runs the startup comparison inside Editor::start. Identity's state, inside identity-web, holds Arc<dyn IdentityRepositories> (identity-core's four ports), the mailer, and OpenWork, through which the depositor-removal confirmation reads open work.

Outside the area the editor depends on shared-metadata (the research-metadata contract), shared-telemetry (the browser beacon) and mosaic-tiles, and on nothing else in the workspace. It never depends on a dpe-* crate: DPE's corpus is consumed as data, an image-baked snapshot handed over as EDITOR_DATA_DIR, never as code (ADR-0002).

Deployment topology and trust boundaries

flowchart TB
  B[Depositor or RDU browser]
  subgraph EO[The editor's own origin]
    T[Traefik] --> S[deposit-server]
    S --> DB[(SQLite volume<br/>working state)]
    S --> PS[Published set,<br/>baked into the image]
  end
  subgraph DO[repository.dasch.swiss, a separate origin]
    DPE[access-server, serving DPE] --> Corpus[Corpus, baked in]
  end
  subgraph GH[GitHub]
    Repo[dsp-repository:<br/>the source of truth]
    Act[GitHub Actions:<br/>editor-pull-requests]
  end
  SMTP[SMTP relay]
  B -->|session cookie, every write a POST with Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin| T
  S -->|login codes, outbound only| SMTP
  Act -->|GET /api/v1/approved-records, public| T
  Act -->|pull request per project, secrets.GH_TOKEN| Repo
  Repo -->|release: the image build bakes the corpus| S
  Repo -->|release| DPE

Five boundaries, and what holds each:

  • Browser to editor. A session comes from a one-time login code sent by mail; there are no passwords. Every state-changing route is POST and passes the Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin check, applied as the outermost layer so no route escapes it. Access is two extractors, Authenticated and Rdu, not a middleware: a handler that names neither is public in its signature (Authentication, Routing).
  • Editor to DPE. Separate deployables on separate origins; see Relationship to DPE.
  • CI to editor. The pull-request run only reads the editor: GET /api/v1/approved-records is public and rate-limited, and nothing is written back. The editor holds no credential at all and makes no outbound GitHub call (Publishing to Git).
  • Editor to repository. Only through the pull request the run opens. The run writes a disposable checkout on its own editor/<shortcode> branch, never in place, and refuses to force-push over a tip it did not write. The pull request is opened with secrets.GH_TOKEN so the repository's checks run on it.
  • Editor to the relay. Outbound only, and no address ever reaches a log (Authentication).

Relationship to DPE

The editor is a separate service from DPE, not a section of it. They share shared-telemetry for the browser-beacon contract, shared-metadata for the research-metadata contract and mosaic-tiles for components — but not a process, an image, or an origin.

The separation is deliberate:

  • DPE is public, unauthenticated and read-only. The editor is authenticated and writes state. A host-level compromise of one should not hand over the other's session cookies.
  • The editor's CSRF defence requires Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin on every state-changing request. On a shared origin, a request originating from DPE is same-origin — so any XSS in DPE, which has a far larger unauthenticated attack surface, could drive authenticated editor mutations. A Path on a cookie is not a security boundary and does not close this.

ADR-0002 records the same choice at the platform level: one modulith per area, never one binary for the whole platform.

Persistence, in one paragraph

Two SQLite databases on a volume, identity.sqlite and editor.sqlite, rusqlite bundled into the static binary. identity-core and editor-core own the records and one repository trait per aggregate; identity-store implements identity's four and editor-store the editor's five, so handlers depend on the ports and not on the driver. The editor's account columns are plain text, not foreign keys, because they point into the other database. Each store has its own pool and migration. A writer pool of exactly one connection and a reader pool of several make the single-writer rule structural, per database: readers are query_only, and the only write path opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Every multi-table transition is one repository method in one transaction. Nothing in either database is irreplaceable (Persistence, Operations).

Rendering and requests, in one paragraph

Server-rendered HTML with Maud, served by Axum, Datastar for enhancement on top of forms that work without it (ADR-0004). Paths are root-mounted on the editor's own hostname. Every write shares its URL with the GET that renders its form and answers two ways, a redirect on the plain path and the changed region as text/html on the enhanced one. Two layers wrap the app, CSRF outermost and OTel inside it, and /healthz and the telemetry beacon are declared after the OTel layers on purpose, so they stay untraced (Routing, Rendering, Observability).

Decisions

  • Platform: the areas and the origin split (ADR-0002), one modulith per area with capabilities behind consumer-defined ports (ADR-0003, amended 2026-09-25 for authentication ports, the area shell and the crate-graph gate, and 2026-10-13 for what a composition root depends on), hypermedia surfaces (ADR-0004), where decision records live (ADR-0006).
  • The editor's own: git as the source of truth (areas/deposit/ADR-0001), the draft as the project's JSON members (areas/deposit/ADR-0002), Online derived at startup (areas/deposit/ADR-0003), and the target shape of the area (areas/deposit/ADR-0004, amended 2026-10-13 for identity-ports, the session deadline in Actor, the web facades and the shell's sign-in link).

Routing and Request Handling

The URL scheme, the method discipline, how a write answers with and without JavaScript, and the two layers that wrap the app.

URL scheme

Paths are root-mounted. There is no /editor prefix.

DPE carries /dpe/… because it shares repository.dasch.swiss with other services. The editor gets its own hostname, so a prefix buys nothing — and adopting one would keep alive the path-routing option this design rejects, for the CSRF reason (Architecture).

PathMethodAccessPurpose
/GETpublic303 to /projects.
/loginGET, POSTpublicThe address form, and issuing a one-time code. POST rate-limited per IP.
/login/codeGET, POSTpublicThe code form, and spending the code. POST rate-limited per IP.
/logoutPOSTpublicDelete the session and clear the cookie.
/projectsGETsigned inThe projects this account may edit, named from the published set.
/projects/{shortcode}GETsigned in + assigned303 to the first form section. 403 otherwise.
/statesGETsigned inWhat each depositor-facing state means and the expected wait before Online (REQ-2.6).
/projects/{shortcode}/sections/{section}GET, POSTsigned in + assignedOne form section, and the save, autosave, submit, withdrawal or discard it makes. 200 even when the project is unpublished.
…/sections/{section}/fields/{field}/addPOSTsigned in + assignedOne more row of a repeatable field. Under the section's URL so it resolves through the same context().
…/sections/{section}/fields/{field}/{key}/removePOSTsigned in + assignedDrop one row. The key is in the path, not a button's name and value, because a programmatic submit omits the submitter's.
/projects/{shortcode}/entities/{proposal}GET, POSTsigned in + assignedOne entity proposal's form, and the save or discard it makes. {proposal} is the proposal's entity_id.
…/entities/{proposal}/fields/{field}/addPOSTsigned in + assignedOne more row of a repeatable field on the entity form.
…/entities/{proposal}/fields/{field}/{key}/removePOSTsigned in + assignedDrop one row, for the reason the section's own row path gives.
/reviewGETRDUThe review queue: every pending submission oldest first, and every draft.
/review/{shortcode}GET, POSTRDUThe field-by-field diff, and the claim, decision save, approve, request-changes or reject it makes.
/depositorsGET, POSTRDUThe account list, and creating a depositor.
/depositors/newGETRDUThe create form.
/depositors/{id}/editGET, POSTRDUThe edit form, and the change it makes.
/depositors/{id}/removeGET, POSTRDUThe removal confirmation, and the removal.
/approvedGETRDUEvery approved record, its status against the published set, and a link to its pull requests on GitHub.
/approved/{id}/discardGET, POSTRDUThe discard confirmation, and the discard.
/healthzGETpublicLiveness probe. Untraced.
/telemetry/collectPOSTpublicBrowser telemetry beacon. Untraced, rate-limited per IP.
/api/v1/approved-recordsGETpublicEvery approved record and its accepted entity proposals, as JSON, for the Pull-request run. Rate-limited per IP.

Everything else is served from the public asset directory, falling back to a 404 rendered in the page shell.

The two row paths are the one exception to the rule below, and deliberately: they are POST-only because both change the form and a GET that did would be a state change on a GET. They never strand a refusal, because they re-render the section rather than redirecting, and a reload of one lands on the section's own GET.

Every write shares a URL with the GET that renders its form, so a rejected submission re-renders somewhere that still answers GET. A write-only path leaves a reloaded rejection at a bare 405, the same dead end the 403 is rendered as a page to avoid.

/ is a redirect rather than a page so that exactly one place decides what a signed-out visitor gets.

There is deliberately no resend endpoint: asking again is another POST /login, under the same cooldown, which keeps the number of endpoints that can send mail at one. See Authentication.

/projects lists the published projects a reader may reach — every project for an RDU member, the intersection of assigned projects and the published set for a depositor. /projects/{shortcode} is a redirect into the form's first section, so exactly one place decides where a project link lands, and there is no per-project landing page between the list and the form. The redirect target is the same section for both audiences — a destination that depended on the role is one more thing to get wrong in a link shared between a depositor and a reviewer.

Two decisions about that scheme:

  • Form sections are real URLs, not fragment swaps. Bookmarkable, Back-friendly, and consistent with the repository's URL-based-navigation principle.
  • Review deep-links by shortcode, not by submission id. A project has at most one pending submission, so the shortcode is unique for the purpose and reads better in a URL shared between reviewers.

The form's two renderings

POST /projects/{shortcode}/sections/{section} is one handler answering two ways, discriminated on the Datastar-Request header the vendored bundle sets on every fetch it makes:

pathoutcomeanswer
no scriptsaved303 to this section's marked GET
no scriptrefused200, the whole page re-rendered at the same URL
Datastarsaved200, the section region as text/html
Datastarrefused200, the same

The plain path redirects because a POST left in the history re-posts on refresh. The enhanced path does not need to and must not: it never navigated, so a refresh re-issues the last GET — and a 303 followed by a full document would hand Datastar an <html> to patch. A refusal re-renders on both paths, because a redirect would throw away what the depositor typed.

That "marked" GET carries a query-string marker the redirect appends: ?saved=<the stored draft's updated_at, RFC 3339, URL-encoded> for a save, or ?done=submitted|withdrawn|discarded for a submit, a withdrawal or a discard. The GET renders the matching notice only while the marker still holds: the stamp still matches the stored row for saved, and for done the project is still in the phase named (locked for submitted, unlocked with the latest round Withdrawn for withdrawn, unlocked with no stored draft for discarded). A stale or bookmarked URL therefore confirms nothing. Because a status region filled at the first load is not reliably announced (editor-web/src/pages/section.rs's module doc argues why), that same GET also prefixes the document <title> with the notice's short form (Draft saved — …, Sent to RDU — …, Submission withdrawn — …, Draft discarded — …), since a navigation does announce a title change where a live region filled at load does not. The entity form (see Entity Proposals) mirrors both halves for its own save (?saved=<the proposal's own stamp>) and discard (?done=discarded), with Saved — … and Discarded — … as its short forms.

Three things about the enhanced path fail quietly if changed:

  • A text/html response is an implicit datastar-patch-elements. With no selector it matches by id in outer mode, so what comes back is the region under one id, not a document.
  • The region is bigger than the form. It is the rail, the status and the form together — everything a save can change. Returning only the <form> leaves the rail showing the obligation counts from before the save, so the depositor fills in the last required field, the field goes quiet, and the rail still says something is missing.
  • A refusal must still answer 200. Datastar processes a response body only on a 200; any other status aborts the fetch and the message the response was carrying never reaches the page. The outcome goes on the span instead, which is where alerting reads it from — the same reasoning as the account forms' redisplayed 200.

data-on:submit carries no __prevent: the bundle calls preventDefault unconditionally for a submit event on a form element, so one would be noise. The form is not novalidate and no field is required, which looks contradictory and is not — see editor-web/src/pages/section.rs, where the type="date" reason is argued.

Request middleware

Two layers wrap the app, in this order from the outside in:

  1. CSRF — Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin is required on every non-GET/HEAD request, failing closed on everything else including an absent header. It is applied last in build_app, which makes it outermost and therefore the one layer the positional traced/untraced split cannot route around: inside build_router it would have missed /telemetry/collect, the only pre-auth POST in the app, with no test failing. See Authentication for why SameSite and __Host- do not close this.
  2. OTel — the traced/untraced split below.

Access control is not a third layer. It is two extractors, Authenticated and Rdu, and that is the design rather than an omission: a handler that names one cannot run without the check, because the argument is what runs it, and a handler that names neither is visibly public at the point anyone reads its signature. A middleware over a sub-router would have added a second positional invariant of exactly the shape this module already regrets — the traced/untraced split is invisible in the route table and reversible by moving one line — and here the failure mode is an unauthenticated route rather than a missing span. See Authentication.

Traced and untraced routes

An Axum layer wraps only routes declared before it. The router therefore has two halves:

  • build_router — everything wrapped by OtelInResponseLayer then OtelAxumLayer. OtelInResponseLayer is declared first so it runs inner and injects the traceparent response header; OtelAxumLayer is declared second so it runs outer and creates the server span.
  • build_app — adds /healthz and /telemetry/collect after those layers, so neither is traced. A liveness probe every 30 seconds and a telemetry upload on every page view would otherwise mint a span each and bury the real traffic.

That split is positional, so it is invisible in the route table and reversible by moving one line. A test asserts /healthz and the beacon are absent from build_router.

Rendering, Datastar and Styling

The view layer's rules: server-rendered Maud, Datastar for enhancement, Tailwind built from explicit source globs.

Rendering model

Same as DPE: server-rendered HTML with Maud, served by Axum, with Datastar for interactivity over SSE. No client-side WASM, no hydration, no islands. The server is the single source of truth for UI state.

Three accessibility decisions the markup depends on

Each of these fails silently: the page renders correctly, and only a screen-reader user or a keyboard user notices.

  • A field's obligation lives inside its own <label> (or <legend>), not beside it. No input carries required or aria-required: a draft may be missing anything and a browser refusing to save one is the opposite of what is asked for. That leaves the accessible name as the only channel the tier has, so a pill rendered as a sibling is visible and nothing else: a reader tabbing to the control hears "Name, edit text". Five control builders compose their own label, so one test asserts the obligation per field across every section rather than on an example; forgetting it in one builder renders identically to a sighted reader.
  • The status region is aria-live="polite" and holds no element with a live role of its own. A refusal renders AlertVariant::Warning rather than Danger for that reason: Danger carries role="alert", an implicit assertive region, and screen readers do not agree on which politeness wins when one is nested inside a polite region — some interrupt, which is the behaviour the polite region exists to avoid. The region announces; the alert only styles.
  • A rail link states its accessible name. The section title and its progress are adjacent <span>s with no whitespace between them, because a flex column is what puts them on two lines — so the name computation concatenates them into "Overview5 of 5 required". The aria-label starts with the visible title, which is what WCAG 2.5.3 asks of an aria-label over visible text, and is omitted for a section with no requirements where the title is already the whole name.

The colour pairings are measured against the design tokens, with the method cross-checked on the four ratios text_field.css already documents: warning-800 on warning-50 11.30:1, info-800 on info-50 11.18:1, neutral-700 on neutral-100 7.78:1, and neutral-600 on the gray-50 page 5.73:1 — all above WCAG 2.1 AA's 4.5:1 for the 12px bold pill text and the hint text.

Datastar

The editor vendors Datastar from areas/deposit/editor/public/vendor/, whose README is the version of record; do not restate the version here. DPE vendors its own copy and is bumped independently.

One thing to get right, and it fails quietly: keyed plugin attributes use :, not - — data-on:click, data-attr:disabled, data-class:open, and data-init rather than data-on-load. This has been true since RC.6, so it matches DPE's markup too. The hyphen form produces a console error and an inert control: the page renders fine and a snapshot test asserting the attribute is present still passes.

Styling

areas/deposit/editor/style/main.css is the single Tailwind entry, built by just css-editor (dev) or just css-editor-release (content-hashed). It imports the design tokens and the mosaic-tiles component barrel.

@import 'tailwindcss' source(none) means classes are collected only from the explicit @source globs, which must cover every crate that emits Tailwind classes. A missing glob produces no build error — just markup whose classes resolve to nothing. After a change that adds classes in a new location, grep the built stylesheet for them.

New Mosaic tiles are added demand-driven: a screen that needs a missing primitive adds it to mosaic-tiles with a playground showcase and a unit test at that point, rather than an up-front form kit. Their CSS goes in mosaic-tiles/src/components/components.css, the barrel every consumer imports.

Check a tile against the surface you are putting it on. Tiles are styled for light backgrounds — link is text-primary-600, which measures 2.35:1 on the footer's bg-slate-800 and fails WCAG 2.1 AA. That is why the footer uses plain anchors inheriting text-gray-300 (9.93:1), as DPE's does. A dark-surface variant of a tile is a design-system change, so it belongs in mosaic-tiles with its own showcase rather than being worked around locally.

Editor Persistence

How the editor stores its working state: two SQLite databases, one per capability, behind the repository ports identity-core and editor-core declare. The decision that nothing in them is irreplaceable is areas/deposit/ADR-0001; the decision to keep one database file per capability is areas/deposit/ADR-0004, "Two databases".

Two SQLite databases, identity.sqlite and editor.sqlite, rusqlite with the bundled feature: the amalgamation is compiled by cc into the binary, which is what keeps the static musl image self-contained. identity-core and editor-core own the records and one repository trait per aggregate; identity-store implements identity's four against identity.sqlite and editor-store the editor's five against editor.sqlite, so handlers depend on the ports and not on the driver. Each store crate has its own copy of the pool module, its own migration module and its own baseline, and neither depends on the other.

rusqlite is pinned to 0.38, not 0.40, because deadpool-sqlite 0.13 (the latest) requires rusqlite ^0.38 and the two cannot coexist: libsqlite3-sys 0.36 and 0.38 both declare links = "sqlite3", so cargo refuses to link both. Bump the pair together once deadpool-sqlite tracks 0.40.

Two pools, and what that buys

Each store's Database holds a writer pool of exactly one connection and a reader pool of several. The split makes two rules structural instead of conventional:

  • Reader connections carry query_only=ON, set in the pool's per-connection init hook, so a write cannot go through Database::read. The only way to write is Database::write, and that always opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE — after which SQLite guarantees nothing up to the matching COMMIT returns SQLITE_BUSY. A deferred BEGIN takes a read lock and can fail to upgrade it at the first write, which surfaces only under concurrency, as database is locked, and looks like something busy_timeout should fix.
  • SQLite allows one writer at a time regardless, so a second writer connection would move the queue out of the pool (a bounded, observable wait) and into SQLite. One writer connection means writes serialise in the pool.

rusqlite::Connection is !Sync. deadpool-sqlite keeps each connection on a thread of its own and only lends it inside an interact closure, so the connection cannot escape, no .await can happen while it is held, and there is no Mutex guard to hold across one. pool.get() is async, so nothing blocks a Tokio worker either. The same shape is why no read transaction outlives a call, which would otherwise starve WAL checkpointing and let -wal grow without bound.

PRAGMAs

All of them are applied in each pool's post_create hook, not once after the pool is built: everything except journal_mode is per-connection state, so central setup would leave every connection after the first at busy_timeout=0 and foreign_keys=OFF while the code read as though they were configured. foreign_keys is set only by identity-store, whose four internal foreign keys need it; the editor schema has no foreign keys. It is a documented silent no-op inside a transaction, so it must never be set from a migration — ON DELETE CASCADE would never fire, orphaned sessions would accumulate against deleted users, and an integrity check would pass because the constraint was never enforced.

File databases get journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=NORMAL; in-memory databases get neither, WAL being a file-database mode.

Schema

Each store has a forward-only list of statement batches guarded by its own PRAGMA user_version, applied at startup — no migration framework and no added dependency. Everything runs in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction including the version bump, so a crash part-way leaves the database at the version it started from. A database reporting a higher version than the build knows stops startup, naming the database: that is a rollback to an older image, and running anyway would query columns that do not exist.

identity.sqlite holds users, user_shortcodes, sessions, login_codes and mail_sends, with four internal foreign keys (three ON DELETE CASCADE, and mail_sends.user_id ON DELETE SET NULL). editor.sqlite holds drafts, submissions, review_rounds, approved_records and entity_proposals. All tables are STRICT, each file created by its store's baseline migration, areas/deposit/identity/store/src/migrations/0001_initial.sql and areas/deposit/editor/store/src/migrations/0001_initial.sql. Their comments carry the reason for each column and index.

The editor's schema has no foreign keys, because it cannot reference a table in another file (areas/deposit/ADR-0004, "Two databases"). The seven account columns, drafts.updated_by, submissions.submitted_by and reviewed_by, review_rounds.actor, approved_records.approved_by and entity_proposals.proposed_by and decided_by, are plain TEXT with their indexes. Deleting an account leaves its id behind, naming no account; pages resolve names through identity and render a miss as unknown.

Until the first production deployment (DEV-6921), a schema change edits the affected store's 0001 in place rather than adding 0002. No database exists that anyone needs to keep, so a numbered migration would record a history nobody lived through. From that deployment on, both 0001 files are frozen and every schema change is a forward migration (0002_*, …) under the same mechanism: the user_version guard never re-runs an applied migration, so an edited 0001 would leave every deployed database on the old shape. Resetting the database on each schema change instead was considered and rejected: the database holds nothing irreplaceable (see Operations), but production keeps it on a volume, and a reset would log everyone out, discard unsubmitted drafts and in-flight reviews, and make RDU re-create every depositor account.

drafts, submissions and approved_records carry their body as an opaque JSON payload string. It holds a serialized editor_core::draft::ProjectDraft, which is #[serde(transparent)] over the project's members, so the column already contains the project object and needs no migration to become typed; the persistence layer never interprets it.

In-memory variant

Selected by leaving EDITOR_DB_DIR unset, which is the default, and it gives two named databases, identity and editor (see Operations for why that is also the preview-safety default). Each is a named shared-cache URI (file:<name>?mode=memory&cache=shared), never bare :memory:: every :memory: database is distinct and visible only to the connection that opened it, so each pooled connection would get its own empty copy, and with a writer/reader split readers could never see anything the writer wrote. The symptom is no such table that comes and goes with pool timing and test order, which reads exactly like a migration bug. Tests use a distinct name per store each, because a shared-cache in-memory database is scoped to the process and parallel cargo test threads share one.

The draft's storage key folds case

drafts.shortcode is an exact-match column, while PublishedProjects::get and Actor::may_reach both fold ASCII case — the published set mixes 080C with 0801a, so a link typed either way reaches the same project. Keying a draft on the path segment as typed would therefore give /projects/080c and /projects/080C a row each for one project, and two people editing it would each keep half the edits with nothing to say so. The section handler folds, in one named place, and is_valid_shortcode admits only ASCII alphanumerics so the fold is total and agrees with the other two by construction.

The Project Representation

What a draft is, where the published set comes from, and how a project file is written. The decision behind the draft's shape is areas/deposit/ADR-0002.

The editor's path is ProjectRaw -> draft -> ProjectRaw, never through DPE's Project view model: impl From<&Project> for ProjectRaw rewrites url into the object form and hardcodes clusters: None, both lossy in exactly the places the editor is required to preserve.

editor_core::draft::ProjectDraft is the project's JSON members rather than a struct mirroring ProjectRaw with 36 Option fields. Three requirements pull that way at once: a draft must hold a field the depositor has not filled in and a value that is present but invalid, it must carry every field the editor does not manage unchanged, and it must survive a field being added to the contract without an editor change. An absent key is a missing field, any value is retained whether it validates or not, and validity is decided once, at to_raw, which is the submission boundary.

The three #[serde(untagged)] enums therefore need no stored variant tag. Untagged deserialization takes the first variant that fits, but a value that keeps its JSON kind verbatim cannot be forced into the wrong one: a string can only be Funding::Text, because Grants needs an array. funding_shape and the two *_shapes accessors derive the variant in serde's own attempt order, so what they report can never disagree with what the written file is built from.

url keeps the form it was read in. Zero of the 85 committed files use the structured object form (36 hold a one-element string array, 38 a two-element array, 11 omit url), so writing the object form would rewrite 74 files. It is used only where there was no prior value: new projects, and those 11 files.

The published set

editor_core::published::PublishedProjects reads $EDITOR_DATA_DIR/projects/*.json once at startup and holds them in memory, keyed by case-folded shortcode. The set cannot change without a redeployment, so nothing polls and nothing invalidates. It is not behind a repository port: the ports exist because the editor writes through them and a test has to be able to make a write fail, and this is a read of an immutable snapshot, so a trait would buy an indirection with one implementation.

Three properties of the committed corpus decide the shape, each measured over all 85 files rather than sampled:

  • The shortcode field is the key, not the filename. Five files disagree with the shortcode they hold — projects/0801_bebb.json is project 0801d, and its siblings under 0801_* are 0801a through 0801e. Keying on the filename stem would file all five under 0801, which no project actually has, so all five would be unreachable by the code they are addressed by and four would be dropped as duplicates.
  • Lookup folds case. 24 shortcodes are mixed case (080C, 081B, 085F), and no two collide when folded. This matches Actor::may_reach, which folds for the same reason. Two files claiming one folded shortcode is reported rather than resolved, so which project answers can never depend on directory order.
  • Nothing about the load is fatal. An unset EDITOR_DATA_DIR is a configured state (the PR preview has no snapshot), and one malformed file among 85 is a problem with the image rather than a reason to refuse every request. Both are reported at warn with a count and one line per failing file, because "84 of 85" is findable where an exited process says only that it exited.

get returning None does not mean the project does not exist. A project may exist only locally, in which case its form opens blank and its pre-fill is empty, so a 404 needs the draft and submission records too — which is why /projects/{shortcode} answers 200 for an unpublished shortcode.

Canonical form

editor_core::canonical::write_project is the single decision about what a projects/*.json file looks like: members in ProjectRaw's declaration order at every depth, null members dropped recursively, language keys alphabetical, four-space indent, a trailing newline, non-ASCII unescaped. An approved submission is then byte-comparable with what is committed, so a review diff shows only what the depositor changed.

Two things make that work and are easy to undo by accident:

  • The workspace enables serde_json's preserve_order. The writer round-trips through serde_json::Value to strip nulls, and Value is BTreeMap-backed without that feature, which would alphabetise every key in every file. Under the feature, Map::remove is swap-remove: use retain or shift_remove.
  • Multilingual fields are shared_metadata::utils::Multilingual (a BTreeMap), not HashMap. Under preserve_order a HashMap field serializes in its own randomised iteration order, which would make the round-trip test flaky.

ProjectRaw deliberately carries no skip_serializing_if: dpe-server's fragments.rs serializes it through axum::Json, so the attribute would drop null members from DPE's API responses too. Stripping happens in the writer instead.

The 85-file round-trip test (editor-core/tests/canonical_round_trip.rs) asserts load -> draft -> write is byte-identical for the whole published corpus, and regenerates it under CANONICALIZE_PROJECT_FILES=1. Generating the corpus from the writer rather than a sibling script is the point: a script has to agree with the writer by inspection, and a near-miss surfaces later as a failing round-trip that looks like a writer bug.

Submission checks

editor_core::submission::unresolved_temporal_coverage applies the rule that every temporalCoverage entry must resolve to a structured date, which access-server validate does not block on and OAI-PMH needs. It reuses shared_metadata::temporal_coverage::completeness_gap, the same decision validate and dpe-api-oai's every_committed_temporal_coverage_resolves apply, and adds the entry index so the form can mark a row rather than the whole field. The open question is settled as refusal: a depositor who needs a period the enrichment table does not know uses the Reference variant, which always resolves — and since the variant chooser landed that escape route is one a depositor can actually take, where before the refusal named a way out the form did not offer.

The Project Form

How the project form decides what it accepts: which fields it insists on, how a reference to a person or an organization is picked, where a fixed vocabulary is a constraint rather than an offer, and what a save refuses. The service's structure is in Architecture; this page is the behaviour that sits on top of it.

Every bound stated here is measured against the 85 committed projects under data/projects/, and the measurements are collected in What the corpus measures at the end, so the source that depends on them has one place to point at.

Obligation is a submit gate, and the corpus bounds which fields carry it

Obligation::Required reads "must be present to submit" and is enforced as written: obligation::unsatisfied_required is what the submit route gates on, and it refuses with one field-level error per unanswered field.

That is only safe because the tier was first bounded by the data. Five of the seventeen fields carrying Required were unsatisfied by the published corpus — all 85 projects lacked documentationMaterial, 13 lacked url, 9 lacked contactPoint, and one each lacked typeOfData and dataLanguage — so a literal gate would have refused every project already live. All five are now Recommended, with the publication requirement moved into the hint where three of them had been claiming "Required before publishing" in words while the pill said the same thing in a tier that could not be enforced.

So the rule is: a field is Required only if the published corpus answers it. obligation's UNANSWERED_BY_THE_CORPUS is empty and its test is now a gate rather than a baseline — tier a field Required that the corpus cannot answer and it fails, naming the field and the count. Fix the tier or fix the data, not the constant.

What the gate adds over the conversion beside it is narrow and worth stating, because the two look redundant: every Required field is a non-Option member of ProjectRaw, so an absent one already fails ProjectDraft::to_raw. The gate catches the state the contract cannot see — present and empty. keywords: [], description: {}, name: "" and a MISSING sentinel all deserialize perfectly well, and none of them is an answer.

Presence is read through obligation::is_satisfied, the same function the section rail counts with. That sharing is deliberate: a gate stricter than the rail would refuse a submission the rail had just counted complete, and a depositor looking at "5 of 5 required" would have no way to tell which of the two was lying. All 85 published projects come out complete for both audiences, which is the same fact stated per project.

The agent store, and how a reference is picked

Three fields hold ids rather than values — contactPoint, attributions[].contributor and funding[].funders — 674 references across the 85 projects. editor_core::agents loads the 558 committed persons and organizations, mirroring PublishedProjects: an explicit load_from returning what loaded plus one error per file. It does not reuse dpe-core's caches, which are a process-wide OnceLock keyed on a global data directory: the editor's directory is EDITOR_DATA_DIR, read into its own EditorState, so a global would make two tests with different fixtures see each other's entities.

Persons and organizations are flattened to one Agent at load time, because every consumer wants exactly an id, a name and a kind from both while the two contract types have different name shapes.

The picker is a server-side search. A row shows who it refers to by name, keeps the id in a hidden input, and offers a search box; the search re-renders that row with its matches as a real <select>, capped at 25, with the current choice first and selected.
